info.title: fusionha
info.description:
fusionha replaces both Sonarr and Radarr with a single app that adds
first-class multi-quality tracking (e.g. 1080p *and* 4K per title) and
treats anime as a first-class citizen. It exposes **two API surfaces**:

* **fusionha-native, `/api/v1/*`** -- the app's own REST API: library items
  (with all their quality editions), settings, config resources (root
  folders, quality profiles, custom formats, indexers, download clients),
  history, queue, health, and blocklist. This is what the fusionha UI (and
  any other fusionha-aware client) talks to.
* **arr v3 mirrors, `/<instance-slug>/api/v3/*`** -- faithful Radarr/Sonarr
  v3 API surfaces (`radarr-hd`, `radarr-4k`, `sonarr-hd`, `sonarr-4k`), each
  its own virtual instance with its own `X-Api-Key`. Add these to
  Overseerr/Seer (their native 4K-service slots map to the `-4k`
  instances) or Prowlarr exactly as you would a real Radarr/Sonarr -- they
  are externally indistinguishable. All virtual instances are views over
  the SAME shared item store; there is no data duplication.

Authenticate against the arr surface with the `X-Api-Key` header (per
virtual instance); see the Authorize button above.

post.description:
“Explore the demo” — a visitor entering the read-only showcase. Lives on the
UNGATED auth router (like login/setup) so it's reachable before any demo
cookie exists. 403 when demo is off; in credentialed mode a wrong/absent
username+password is 401; on success it sets the demo cookie so `require_user`
admits the caller as the read-only DemoPrincipal. Open mode accepts any body.
Leave the demo (clear the demo cookie). Ungated — always safe.

get.description:
The current caller's identity.

Accepts EVERY principal `require_user` accepts, which it previously did not:
it resolved the session cookie ONLY, so a caller holding the `app_api_key`
could drive every gated `/api/v1` route yet got a 401 here. Since the SPA
treats a 401 from this endpoint as "signed out", that made the whole UI
unreachable to a key holder -- an automated browser check could exercise the
API but never a screen. The key already authorises the same data through
`require_user`, so answering here grants no new authority; it removes an
inconsistency.

The key is deliberately IDENTITY-LESS (`TrustedKeyPrincipal`: break-glass,
allow-all), so there is no user row to return. Rather than invent a fake one,
it reports a synthetic non-human identity: `id=0` (no user can hold 0) and a
username that reads as a machine. `is_admin` is True because the trusted key
already bypasses `require_admin` everywhere else -- claiming otherwise here
would be the response lying about what the caller can do.

post.description:
Mint a Plex PIN and return the interactive `authUrl` (spec §8). 404 when
Plex sign-in is disabled; a Plex outage is a friendly 502, never a 500.

Binds the pin to THIS browser via a short-lived HttpOnly cookie so only the
originator may later `check` it (account-takeover / login-CSRF defense).

Poll a PIN (spec §8). Pending -> `202 {status:"pending"}`; authorised +
admitted -> mint the `fusionha_session` cookie and return `UserRead`;
authorised + not a member -> `403`; a disabled account -> `403`. 404 when
Plex sign-in is disabled.

ORIGINATOR BINDING (security fix): a request lacking the matching pin cookie
(set by `create_plex_pin`) gets the SAME `202 pending` a truly-pending pin
returns -- so a non-originator can neither steal the minted session nor tell a
real pin_id from a bogus one (enumeration oracle removed).

post.description:
LF-B4: probe the LIVE effective TMDB key (DB > env) with a cheap
authenticated `/configuration` call. Returns `{ok, message}` -- a 401/
invalid key or a network error yields `ok:false` with a friendly message,
never a 500/stack trace, and the key is never echoed.

#180: probe the LIVE effective TVDB key (+ optional PIN) with a fresh
``POST /login``. Returns ``{ok, message}`` -- a missing key, an invalid
key/PIN (401/403), or a network error yields ``ok:false`` with a friendly
message, never a 500/stack trace, and the credentials are never echoed.

Short-transaction discipline: the key+PIN are read up front and the read
transaction is released (``session.rollback()``) BEFORE the login HTTP, so
the pooled DB connection is never held across the network round-trip. The
login itself uses a short-lived, loop-local ``HttpxClient`` (closed after the
single call), never the shared main-loop ``app.state.http`` pool.

Plex SSO: validate the configured owner token (spec §8). Resolves the
owner identity + owned server + membership set, persists the resolved
``plex_server_machine_id``/``plex_server_name``, and returns
``{ok, owner_username, server_name, machine_id, member_count}``. A missing
token, an invalid token, or a network error yields ``ok:false`` with a
friendly message -- never a 500/stack trace, and the token is never echoed.

Short-transaction discipline (mirrors ``test-tvdb``): the token +
client-identifier are read up front and the read transaction is released
(``session.rollback()``) BEFORE the HTTP round-trips, over a short-lived
loop-local :class:`HttpxClient` (closed after), never the shared
``app.state.http`` pool.

Plex SSO: run the shared-users import on demand (spec §8) -> the number of
members provisioned as Requestors this run. Already-provisioned (possibly
elevated) members are left untouched.

Short-transaction + no-leak discipline (mirrors ``test-plex``): the read
transaction is released (``session.rollback()``) BEFORE the Plex round-trips,
which run over a short-lived, loop-local :class:`HttpxClient` closed in a
``finally`` -- never the shared main-loop ``app.state.http`` pool, and never
holding the request's DB transaction across the network. ``import_shared_users``
does all network I/O first, then the DB writes.

Plex SSO: PRUNE (DELETE) auto-provisioned Requestor accounts that can no
longer sign in -> ``{removed, usernames}``. Explicit on-demand counterpart to
the ``plex_prune_on_import`` toggle.

DANGER: this deletes user accounts, so the guards are strict (see
:meth:`PlexSsoService.prune_ineligible`): only auto-provisioned
(``auth_provider == "plex"``) Requestors whose Plex identity is no longer in
the LIVE login-admitted membership set are removed -- LINKED accounts, elevated
accounts, and the owner are NEVER touched -- via the SAME deletion path the
manual delete-user endpoint uses. **FAIL-SAFE:** if the live Plex membership
fetch fails, NOTHING is deleted (a friendly 502, empty result).

Short-transaction + no-leak discipline (mirrors ``plex-import``): the read
transaction is released (``session.rollback()``) BEFORE the Plex round-trips,
which run over a short-lived, loop-local :class:`HttpxClient` closed in a
``finally`` -- never the shared main-loop pool, never holding a DB txn across
the network.

get.description:
LF-B5: reveal the current fusionha native app API key (unchanged) so an
operator can copy it for use as an `X-Api-Key` header. Generates it on
first read if one does not exist yet.

SECURITY: gated on FULL admin, NOT `settings.manage`. The app_api_key
resolves to the allow-all `TrustedKeyPrincipal` (god-mode break-glass), so a
non-admin `settings.manage` holder who could read it would bypass every admin
gate -- revealing it is therefore an admin-only privilege.

post.description:
LF-B5: rotate the fusionha native app API key and return the new value.
The previous key stops authorizing `X-Api-Key` requests immediately.

SECURITY: FULL admin only (see `reveal_app_api_key`) -- the returned key is
the allow-all break-glass credential, so minting/reading it is admin-only.

Plex SSO admin auto-config: mint a Plex PIN and return the interactive
``authUrl`` the admin's browser opens to authorise this device (spec §8). The
admin-gated twin of the public ``/auth/plex/pin`` create. A Plex outage is a
friendly 502, never a 500; the token is captured later on
``/settings/plex/connect/{id}/check``.

Binds the pin to THIS browser via a short-lived HttpOnly cookie so only the
originator may later ``check`` it (account-takeover / login-CSRF defense).

Plex SSO admin auto-config: poll a connect PIN (spec §8). Still pending ->
``202 {status:"pending"}`` (nothing persisted); authorised -> capture the
token, resolve the owner identity + owned server, PERSIST the token +
``plex_server_machine_id``/``plex_server_name``, and return
``status="connected"`` with the resolved public facts + best-effort member
count. An account with no owned server is a 400 (nothing persisted); a Plex
outage is a friendly 502. The captured token becomes the owner token -- never
logged, redacted out of ``/settings`` as ``plex_owner_token_set``.

ORIGINATOR BINDING (security fix): a request lacking the matching pin cookie
(set by ``plex_connect_create_pin``) gets the SAME ``202 pending`` a
truly-pending pin returns -- so a non-originator can neither capture a token
into config nor probe pin_ids.

Read custom formats + quality profiles from a live Sonarr/Radarr and
import them (``source="arr"``). The API key is never echoed back.

post.description:
Test an UNSAVED indexer config (the "Test" button before Save).

Accepts the full create body, builds a transient (never-added)
`SearchIndexer`, and runs the same lightweight caps probe as the saved-row
test -- persisting nothing. Tests inject a `FakeHttpClient`, so no socket
opens under test.

INDEXER-WIRING-BE: re-mirror every Prowlarr-pushed arr.Indexer into
``search_indexers`` on demand.

Indexers Prowlarr pushed while ``real_integrations`` was off were never
mirrored (the upsert path only syncs when the flag is on), so they are
stranded -- present as arr.Indexer rows but unsearchable until Prowlarr
re-pushes. This endpoint (and the same backfill on the off->on settings
flip) makes them searchable immediately. Idempotent and
provenance-respecting: re-running never duplicates a row nor clobbers a
user's ``manual`` row (see ``backfill_search_indexers``).

CAPS-AWARE SEARCH: after mirroring, best-effort fetch each newly/previously
caps-unknown row's ``t=caps`` <searching> advertisement (the sync upsert can
not -- it has no HTTP seam), so Prowlarr-derived rows gain capability-aware
query routing instead of the safe id-mode default.

schema.title: Response List Search Indexers Api V1 Searchindexers Get

post.description:
Test an UNSAVED notification agent config (the "Test" button before
Save). Accepts the full create body, builds a transient (never-added)
`NotificationAgent`, and sends the canned test notification -- persisting
nothing. Tests inject a `FakeHttpClient`, so no socket opens under test.

get.description:
Every `ArrNotification`, grouped by the virtual instance it lives on.
Secrets redacted; ordered by instance then registration id so a duplicate
on one instance is visible as two rows.

post.description:
Create a user-configured Webhook connection on one virtual instance,
via the same `apply_notification_payload` path the arr
`/api/v3/notification` POST route uses -- the persisted `fields` shape
stays byte-for-byte decypharr-compatible.

delete.description:
Remove one arr-registered connection (e.g. a stale/duplicate decypharr
registration). Display+delete only -- fusionha never *creates* an arr
webhook (the external tool owns that lifecycle).

put.description:
Update an existing connection (any source -- including one a user
created here, or a stray external registration an admin wants to
correct). A blank/absent `password` preserves the stored secret; the
`fields` list is rebuilt through `apply_notification_payload` exactly as
the arr PUT route would, so re-reading it via GET /notification on the
owning virtual instance shows the identical shape.

post.description:
Fire a real outbound arr 'Test' event at the webhook's configured URL
(`ArrDownloadNotifier.notify_test`) and report the live result -- unlike
every other `notify_*` dispatch this is NOT best-effort/fire-and-forget,
the Test button needs the real 2xx/failure to show the user.

Test an UNSAVED download-client config (the "Test" button before Save).

Accepts the full create body, builds a transient (never-added)
`DownloadClientConfig`, and runs the same version/login probe as the
saved-row test -- persisting nothing.

get.description:
List quality definitions.

Without ``media_kind``: the SHARED defaults (the NULL-kind rows) -- one
row per quality, exactly the pre-override list shape every existing
consumer (Quality Definitions panel, Manage-Episodes quality picker)
expects. With ``media_kind``: that kind's EFFECTIVE set -- per quality,
the kind's override row when one exists, else the shared default -- so a
client can render a kind's windows and tell overridden (``media_kind``
set) from inherited (NULL). Every row stays reachable: each override
surfaces (with its id) in its own kind's effective view.

get.description:
List login identities. Tombstoned (merged-away) accounts -- an identity
that was consolidated into a survivor via a merge (``merged_into`` set) -- are
EXCLUDED by default so the collapsed duplicate disappears from the table; pass
``?include_merged=true`` for the audit/forensics view.

schema.title: Response List Users Api V1 Users Get

get.description:
READ-ONLY likely-duplicate suggestions for an admin to review before a
merge (spec §Auto-link-vs-admin-merge). NEVER auto-links -- it only surfaces
groups by three heuristics: same case-insensitive email; the ``(plex:<id>)``
disambiguated twin of a bare local username; an identical normalised handle.

Declared BEFORE ``/users/{user_id}`` so ``duplicates`` is not swallowed by the
``{user_id}`` int path param (which would 422).

Same-origin proxy for a user's Plex profile picture.

The stored ``user.thumb`` is a ``plex.tv`` URL that the SPA's CSP ``img-src
'self'`` blocks, so the avatar would never render cross-origin. This endpoint
fetches the picture server-side and streams it back from fusionha's own origin
(covered by CSP ``self``) -- so the CSP need NOT be widened to plex.tv.

Gate: ``require_user`` (any signed-in user may see avatars). BEST-EFFORT: no
thumb, an SSRF-refused thumb, or any upstream error/timeout -> ``404`` (the
frontend falls back to initials); it never 500s. The bytes carry the upstream
``content-type`` (default ``image/jpeg``) and a one-day public cache header.

post.description:
Force sign-out: delete this account's live sessions WITHOUT disabling it
(the account stays enabled and its PATs keep working) -- the one-shot
counterpart to the lasting `is_active=False` block.

A real, non-admin caller may only revoke its OWN sessions. Acting on ANOTHER
account needs `users.manage` (mirrors change-password's self-vs-privileged
split). For a SELF revoke the caller's CURRENT session is preserved -- "sign
out my other devices" must not log the caller out mid-request; a privileged
revoke of another account clears every session.

Start linking a Plex identity to this account: mint a Plex PIN and return
the interactive ``authUrl`` the browser opens to authorise this device. The
completion happens on ``.../plex/link/{id}/check``.

Self-or-``users.manage`` gated (a user links its own account; an admin may link
another). Independent of ``plex_sso_enabled`` -- linking works whether or not
Plex SSO login is turned on. A Plex outage is a friendly 502, never a 500.

Binds the pin to THIS browser via a short-lived HttpOnly cookie so only the
originator may later ``check`` it (account-takeover / login-CSRF defense).

Poll a link PIN. Still pending (or a request lacking the matching pin cookie
-- same 202 so a non-originator can neither complete a link nor probe pin_ids)
-> ``202 {status:"pending"}`` (nothing stamped). Authorised -> resolve the Plex
identity and stamp it onto the TARGET account (``plex_user_id`` /
``plex_username`` / ``thumb``; ``email`` only when the account has none),
leaving ``auth_provider`` unchanged (stays ``"local"`` = dual-auth, the account
keeps its password). Returns the updated :class:`UserRead`.

Self-or-``users.manage`` gated. A Plex account already linked to a DIFFERENT
fusionha account is a 409 (nothing stamped). A Plex outage is a friendly 502.

Remove the Plex identity from this account (clears ``plex_user_id`` /
``plex_username`` / ``thumb``). The account, its role, password and email are
untouched -- it simply can no longer sign in with Plex. Self-or-``users.manage``
gated.

get.description: List a person's sign-in methods (NO secret). Self-or-``users.manage``.

schema.title: Response List Credentials Api V1 Users  User Id  Credentials Get

post.description:
Add (or reset) a password for this person -- the "add-a-password to a
Plex-first account" feature.

``provider`` (``local``) and ``external_id`` (``lower(username)``) are ALWAYS
server-derived (INV2); the body carries only the password. Creates the ``local``
credential where a Plex-first person had none, and keeps ``users.password_hash``
in sync (via ``AuthService.set_password``). Gate: self OR (full ``system.admin``
+ amplification guard) (INV3).

delete.description:
Detach a sign-in method. Refuses removing the identity's LAST ACTIVE
credential (INV7 -- would lock the person, incl. the last enabled admin, out).
On success revokes the identity's live sessions (INV5) and clears the matching
``users`` shadow column. Gate: self OR (full ``system.admin`` + amplification)
(INV3).

patch.description:
Set a credential's ``is_primary`` (reconciled to exactly one per person) and/
or ``is_active``. Disabling (``is_active=false``) fails the credential closed at
login, revokes the identity's live sessions (INV5), and is refused when it would
leave the person with zero active credentials (INV7). ``provider``/
``external_id``/``secret`` are never settable here (INV2). Gate: self OR (full
``system.admin`` + amplification) (INV3).

post.description:
Fold ``loser`` into ``survivor`` (or preview it with ``dry_run``).

FULL ``system.admin`` only (INV3/INV4). ``dry_run=true`` returns the EFFECTIVE
resulting privilege set + row-movement summary + any blockers, mutating
nothing; ``dry_run=false`` refuses on any blocker (last-admin/amplification/
plex-conflict) else performs the single-transaction merge and emits a
``user.merge`` audit event. The operator is expected to have taken a backup
before an execute (the backup is operator-side).

Re-point one credential from ``user_id`` onto ``target_user_id``.

FULL ``system.admin`` (INV3) AND amplification-checked against the TARGET
(binding a login path into it, exactly like the Plex link path). Refuses
stripping the source's last active credential (INV7) or moving a Plex identity
onto a target that already holds a different one. Revokes the source's live
sessions (INV5) and emits a ``user.credential.move`` audit event.

Remove a whole provider (e.g. ``plex``) across every identity.

FULL ``system.admin`` only. ``dry_run`` previews the affected identities;
execute applies the chosen ``fallback`` for any identity left with no sign-in
method (``disable``/``delete``, or ``password`` which REFUSES a would-be-zeroed
identity), refuses if it would remove the last enabled admin, revokes affected
sessions (INV5), and emits a ``user.credential.disconnect`` audit event.

Declared as a fixed ``/users/credentials/disconnect`` path (no ``{user_id}``)
so it is never swallowed by the parametrised credential routes.
Mint a token; the raw secret is returned ONCE in `TokenMintRead.token`.

get.description:
List token metadata.

A self-service caller (the common case) sees ONLY its own tokens. A
`users.manage` holder may pass `?user_id=` to list another user's tokens;
an identity-less allow-all caller (auth-off / trusted key) with no
`user_id` sees ALL tokens.

schema.title: Response List Tokens Api V1 Tokens Get

delete.description: Revoke a token (delete-row). Owner deletes own; else needs `users.manage`.

post.description:
Submit a request for a title at one-or-more editions (P2a).

422 when an edition is not allowed by the user's policy; 403 when an edition
is outside the caller's access scope (policy ∩ per-instance visibility); 409
when EVERY requested edition is already owned. An open request for the same
title MERGES (union editions/seasons/episodes) rather than 409. Auto-approve
(policy) runs the real add when the full edition set is auto-approved.

A genuinely NEW request row fires the REQUEST_MADE Web Push alert (admins/
managers) best-effort in the background — never on a no-op merge
re-request, and never able to fail the submission itself.

get.description:
List requests.

A caller sees ONLY its own requests by default; a `requests.approve` holder
(and the allow-all Anonymous/app-key principals, which authorize every
permission) sees ALL. Derived purely from the permission — NOT from
`caller is None`, so a read-only Demo visitor (require_user returns None but
the principal is a non-approving DemoPrincipal) does NOT see everyone's
requests. `status` filters on the STORED status (the derived `fulfilled` is a
read-time projection, not a stored value to filter on).

schema.title: Response List Requests Api V1 Requests Get

get.description:
The editions the CURRENT principal may request for `(kind, tmdb_id)`.

Access-scoped: policy-allowed ∩ per-instance-visible ∩ not-already-owned, so
the request modal renders only these (or, in `auto` mode, the admin-fixed set
with no picker). Gated by the same `request` capability as `POST /requests`.
Defined before the `/requests/{request_id}/…` routes so the static path wins.

post.description:
Approve a request — the real resolveTier add: creates/links the edition,
monitors it, and links `media_item_id`. A 2nd-tier approve on an owned title
ADDS an edition, never a duplicate item.

The OPTIONAL body carries the approve dialog's edition picker: `editions` is
extra editions/variants to enable on the same item in one action (the
requested tier is always ensured regardless — it is locked-on), and `search`
fires a per-edition background search over exactly the editions this approve
created (never the already-owned siblings). No body / no `editions` = the
plain approve (requested tier only), backward-compatible.

A real user may NOT approve its OWN request (403); the identity-less allow-all
principals have no identity to collide, so they pass. 422 when no Add-defaults
root/profile is configured for the requested kind·tier.
Reject (or defer) a request with a REQUIRED reason (`defer=True` -> deferred).

delete.description:
Withdraw (delete) a request. The requester deletes its own; a
`requests.approve` holder may delete any; an identity-less allow-all caller
passes; anyone else is 403.

get.description:
The user's request policy. A user with no policy row reports the permissive
default (empty tier lists = no restriction, unlimited quota).

put.description:
Upsert the user's request policy. Absent fields keep their stored value;
tier lists are stored as `QualityTier` member NAMES.

post.description:
Report a problem with an on-server title.

404 when the item does not exist; 422 on a season/episode scope missing its
coordinates; 403 when a request-scoped reporter files on a title it never
requested. The reporter is ALWAYS the calling principal's user — an
identity-less allow-all caller (auth-off / trusted app key) has no session
identity, so it may not create an issue (400).

get.description:
List issues. A caller sees ONLY its own by default; an ``issues.manage``
holder (and the allow-all Anonymous/app-key principals) sees ALL. ``status``
filters on the stored status.

schema.title: Response List Issues Api V1 Issues Get

post.description: Resolve an issue with an optional note. Gated by ``issues.manage``.

delete.description:
Withdraw (delete) an OPEN issue. The reporter deletes its OWN open issue;
an ``issues.manage`` holder deletes any; an identity-less allow-all caller
passes; anyone else is 403. A RESOLVED issue is history and is not
withdrawable by its reporter (409) — a manager may still delete it.

get.description:
The browser ``applicationServerKey``. Provisions the keypair on first use.

Authed but NOT admin -- every user needs it to subscribe. Only the PUBLIC
key is exposed; the private key never leaves the server.

post.description:
Register a device, bound to the caller. UPSERT keyed on device identity.

Identity precedence is ``(user_id, device_id)`` when the client sends a
stable ``device_id`` (a UUID minted in the browser's IndexedDB), so a rotated

(client-completion check → readability/sample probe → import incl.

The bind is captured ON the loop (cheap, no query) BEFORE offloading; the pass
itself runs on a worker thread over its OWN session (never blocking HTTP) and

``IMPORT_POLL_LIMITER`` so the two can't mutate the same downloads
concurrently. ``real_integrations`` off returns HTTP 200 with ``skipped=true``
(a queue pass has nothing to do with integrations disabled) -- never a 5xx; an

post.description:
Bulk-set the Radarr per-movie minimum availability on the selected
targets' MOVIE editions only (announced|inCinemas|released, validated by the
`MinimumAvailability` enum -> 422 on anything else). A SERIES edition in the
selection is left untouched -- `minimum_availability` is a movie-only
attribute (its column stays NULL) -- and is not counted in `affected`.
Availability is computed on READ (`movie_is_available`), so persisting the
new value is all that's needed; no recompute follows. Reuses the shared
`_resolve_editions` selection machinery + one-commit-per-request boundary.

#112: tier-scoped, VERIFIED bulk root re-assign.

Per selected item, resolve the editions OF ``payload.tier`` (the tier column
already groups a standard with its variants -- both carry that tier, so a
plain ``edition.tier == tier`` match keeps the standard and its variants
together and never separated); ``tier="all"`` is the warned escape hatch that
hits every edition. An item with no edition of the tier is SKIPPED (counted).

Each resolved edition routes through the SAME #96 verified move
(:func:`change_edition_root` -> ``_move_pairs`` stage->verify->remove) honoring
``disposition`` -- NEVER a bare ``root_folder_id`` assignment (the old
silent-orphan bug). A per-edition failure is captured and reported and does
NOT abort the batch: each successful edition is committed on its own so a
later failure can never roll back an already-relocated file's DB flip.

#150: bulk "Refresh & Scan" -- open a run per selected item and dispatch
each as a background task, exactly like the single-item
``POST /library/{id}/refresh`` (:func:`library_detail_routes.refresh_item`).

Each found item opens its own ``CommandRun`` (RUNNING) and hands the heavy
work to
:func:`~fusionha.api.library_detail_routes._spawn_refresh_task`; the runs
QUEUE on the existing #150 ``_refresh_scan_gate`` automatically (at most
``REFRESH_SCAN_CONCURRENCY`` execute at once, the rest await a slot) -- no new
locking here. The endpoint returns ``202`` immediately; it does NOT wait for
the work. An ``item_id`` matching no item is counted in ``errors`` and skipped,
never raised as a 500.

WHOLE-LIBRARY FORCE GUARD: a FORCE refresh (``metadata_only`` False) over more
than :data:`MAX_FORCE_REPROBE_ITEMS` items is refused (422) -- a select-all
force across a cold mount is the one path to the days-long re-sweep incident,
so it is made impossible rather than silently weakened. ``metadata_only``
refreshes never probe and are never capped.

`remove_edition_files` helper (T19/T34) before dropping the item; the

`quality_editions` with no `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so before dropping the
item this explicitly purges every dependent row for the item AND its
editions (`purge_dependent_rows`) -- otherwise the delete either 500s
(FK pragma on) or orphans those rows.

exists because the edit dialog only sends `series_type` when the value

`ArrScopeMismatchCheck` health warning both drop; a LATER add through an

`POST .../editions`). Scoped to the owning item -- an edition id that isn't
THIS item's is a 404.

A title must keep at least one edition (CLAUDE.md #2: HD 1080p is the
default edition; a zero-edition item has nothing to monitor/grab), so
deleting the LAST remaining edition is refused (400) -- use
`DELETE /{item_id}` to drop the whole title. `deleteFiles=true` recycles/

row is dropped, mirroring `delete_item` but for a single edition -- the
item and its sibling editions survive untouched.

detail screen's "add a 4K edition" (or, for a movie, a second cut) action.

The multi-quality defining feature (CLAUDE.md #2): a title is one logical
item that can carry multiple independently-tracked editions. This is the
native counterpart to the arr add path -- both go through the SAME

monitoring identically (same `monitored`/`monitor`/`minimum_availability`),

(`edition_wants_episode`): `apply_series_monitor` re-derives the season/

once.

Guards: unknown item -> 404; a `movie_edition` is accepted on either kind
(#115: on a series it is the "version" -- Colour / Black & White); a
duplicate `(tier, movie_edition)` -> 409; a
quality profile whose kind is incompatible with the item (#55) or an

post.description:
#62 Phase 3: on-demand "Check for 4K now" -- run a single-item, OBSERVE-ONLY
probe for this title's 2160p availability. Unlike the scheduled discovery
probe this EXPLICIT user action spends a query against ALL enabled+capable
indexers regardless of their daily budget (it still respects the per-indexer
IndexerThrottle spacing + a 429 cool-off), then records what it saw. It NEVER
grabs. Returns the fresh genuine (non-upscale) availability for the item.

ITEMACTIONS-BE: the detail toolbar's "Refresh & Scan" (backgrounded, #136).

Opens a ``CommandRun`` (RUNNING) and IMMEDIATELY returns ``202 {run_id}``; the
heavy work runs in a tracked background task (:func:`_refresh_dispatch`) so a
multi-season rescan never blocks the HTTP response past the gateway edge
timeout. The frontend polls ``/system/runs/{run_id}`` for live progress and,
on completion, the ``rescan_summary``.

The backgrounded task re-fetches the item's TMDB detail and writes it back via
the SAME `apply_item_metadata` the add path uses; for a series it also
re-syncs episode titles/air-dates and (when a live HTTP client is wired and
TVmaze is enabled) fills episode air-times. The metadata fetch is best-effort.
Unless `?metadata_only=true`, it then re-scans each edition's root folder to
re-detect files (attach newly-found, prune confirmed-gone).

The run is opened on the REQUEST session (so the 202 carries a real, pollable
``run_id``) but the background task opens its OWN session for the work -- this
request session closes the moment we return.

Per-season "Refresh & Scan" for a series (backgrounded, #136 + #A).

The same pipeline as the item-level :func:`refresh_item` but SCOPED to one
season: the metadata re-sync targets that season's episodes and the disk
re-scan's expensive phases (folder discovery/adopt + the ffprobe/MediaInfo
re-probe) are limited to the season's folder + files, so a big series can
refresh a single season without probing all of them. Rejects a movie (no
seasons) and an unknown season number. Returns ``202 {run_id}`` like the
item refresh; progress polls the same ``/system/runs/{run_id}`` channel.

#180 Fix B: the MANUAL escape hatch for the corroborated tvdb_id backfill --
run the resolver against ONE series on demand and, on a confident match,
persist the id.

The "never guess; surface for manual" contract's user-initiated path: the
scheduled backfill fills what it can corroborate unattended; this lets a user
resolve a specific stranded series now. Writes ``tvdb_id`` ONLY where it is
still NULL (re-asserted in the UPDATE WHERE -- never overwrites an existing id,
even if the resolver returns a different one). KEY-ONLY gated like the manual
TVDB numbering compare (a configured key is all it needs; NOT the tvdb_enabled
toggle). Returns the resolved id + source, or ``matched=false`` + a reason.

get.description:
#111 P6 / #180 P4: preview what an episode-numbering override to ``source``
WOULD change -- read-only (like ``check-4k``), no persist. Returns the season-
by-season diff, the projected file re-link summary (moved/unparseable), the
phantom disposition, whether an active queue would block the apply, the
RESOLVED compare source, and a ``diff_hash`` the client echoes on
``POST .../numbering/apply`` so a stale preview can never be blind-applied.

Source-resolution contract (must MATCH the apply route so the ``diff_hash``
re-check can never 409 wrongly): when the client OMITS ``source`` (``None``,
the default) the effective source is derived from the series' resolved
metadata provider via :func:`default_numbering_source` (tvdb/hybrid -> tvdb,
else tvmaze). An explicit valid ``source`` the client PINS always wins (so the
UI can offer an override).

Cleanly handles a non-series item, an unknown source, and a fetch failure
(unresolvable show / empty payload / no TVDB key or tvdb_id) -- always a 4xx,
never a 500. Gated behind ``require_user`` at router inclusion
(``api/app.py``).

post.description:
#111 P6: admin-gated apply of an episode-numbering override (mirrors the
refresh background-run scaffolding, ``dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)]``
like ``api/instances_routes.py``).

Recomputes the diff SERVER-SIDE (a fresh current tree + a fresh fetch of the
resolved alternate source -- TVmaze or TVDB, #180 P4) and 409s when its hash
disagrees with the client's ``expected_hash``
-- a stale preview (the series/source changed since it was rendered) can
never be blind-applied. Also refuses (409) when the series already has an
active queue -- an in-flight grab could import onto stale numbering mid-
renumber. Both checks run HERE, synchronously, before a ``CommandRun`` is
even opened, so a rejected apply commits nothing and never shows up in the
run feed. Only once both pass does the actual renumber+relink run as a
BACKGROUND run (``202 {run_id}``), polled via ``GET /system/runs/{run_id}``
for its ``numbering_summary`` once terminal; ``apply_numbering`` re-checks
both guards internally as defence-in-depth against the tiny race between
this check and the background task actually running.

#111 P6: admin-gated clear of the numbering override -- reversible-by-
design (:func:`services.episode_numbering_apply.reset_numbering`). Leaves
every episode row/file exactly as it stands; the next metadata refresh
re-adopts TMDB numbering.

(recovered from the on-disk symlink target) to the episode(s) it is currently

left with no file, and source-collision -- WITHOUT any write.

Independent of a numbering diff: this is for the case where the episode
numbers are already correct but the FILES sit on the wrong episodes (the 1086
'2 Broke Girls' shape after a numbering switch). Non-series / missing item ->
422/404.

post.description:
Admin-gated apply: re-map every mislinked series file onto the episode its
symlink-target content identity actually is, then rename the on-disk symlinks
to match (debrid-safe). Reuses the collision-safe machinery of the numbering
apply -- a source-collision is surfaced as a ``conflict`` and NEVER silently
merged. Non-series / missing item -> 422/404.

#43 (v5): a READ-ONLY diff of switching this series' metadata source to
``target_provider`` -- the confirmed/needs-search target match, the
season/episode reconcile, the per-file raw matching + confidence, and a
``diff_hash`` the commit echoes back. No writes. Movies are TMDB-only (422).
Bounded/off-loop: the diff + parse-heavy file matching run in a worker thread
(mirrors ``_rescan_offloaded``).

#43 (v5): admin-gated COMMIT of a reviewed metadata-source switch. Re-derives
the diff SERVER-SIDE (fresh target fetch) and 409s on a stale ``expected_hash``;
refuses (409) with an active queue. Both checks run HERE before a run opens, so
a rejected switch commits nothing. The renumber+relink+refresh+rename then runs
as a BACKGROUND run (``202 {run_id}``, polled for ``metadata_switch_summary``).
"Switch only, keep filenames" = ``rename_files=false`` (still a completed
commit -- the provider IS set).

provider + numbering + on-disk filenames from the stored snapshot. Offloaded
(it moves files). 409 when the snapshot is gone / an active queue blocks it.

"Search missing only" / "Search each episode" rows.

The item-level counterpart to ``.../season/{n}/gradual``: it collects the
MISSING + UPGRADEABLE + MONITORED, already-aired episodes across EVERY monitored
season (optionally scoped to one ``edition_id`` across all its seasons) and
searches them ONE AT A TIME, spaced by ``season_search_interval_seconds``, in a
background task under ONE ``CommandRun`` spanning the whole title -- returning
``{run_id, total}`` immediately so the frontend polls ``/system/runs/{run_id}``.

``missing_only`` (#76) scopes it to fileless episodes only (skips cutoff-unmet
upgrades). ``edition_id`` scopes to one edition across all its seasons (the
edition-card rows); omit it for the whole title / every monitored edition (the
Wanted rows). Refuses (409) when a whole-title job OR ANY per-season gradual job
for this item is already in flight -- the two scopes must never both run (they
would double-search an episode). ``total == 0`` (``run_id: null``) when there is
nothing to search.

#76: STOP an in-flight WHOLE-TITLE gradual search. Sets the job's cancel flag
so the loop stops BEFORE its next episode (the current episode's search, if any,
finishes; the run then closes INTERRUPTED). Idempotent -- ``canceled: false``
with ``run_id: null`` when no item-level gradual job is running for this item.
404 only when the item itself doesn't exist.

#91: START the "Search each episode (gradual)" mode for a season.

#76: ``missing_only`` scopes the SAME gradual per-episode process to just the
fileless (missing) episodes, skipping cutoff-unmet upgrade targets -- the
"Search missing only" menu row. Both modes are gradual; they differ only in
scope.

Unlike the default season Search (one season-pack decision, POST
``/library/{id}/search?season=N``), this searches the season's MISSING +
UPGRADEABLE (present file below the profile cutoff / CF-score ceiling) +
MONITORED, already-aired episodes ONE AT A TIME, spaced by
``season_search_interval_seconds``, in a background task -- returning
``{run_id, total}`` immediately so the frontend polls
``/system/runs/{run_id}`` for live per-episode progress + a Stop. Searching an
upgradeable present episode is data-safe: the grab decision engine grabs ONLY a
genuine upgrade over the existing file, never a downgrade/sidegrade.

Scoped to the monitored editions (or an explicit ``edition_id``), mirroring
how the season-pack search scopes. Refuses (409) a second gradual job for the
same ``(item, season)`` while one is in flight, echoing the in-flight run.
``total == 0`` (with ``run_id: null``) when there is nothing to search (zero
missing AND zero cutoff-unmet -- all episodes meet the cutoff).

#91: STOP an in-flight gradual season search. Sets the job's cancel flag so
the loop stops BEFORE its next episode (the current episode's search, if any,
finishes; the run then closes INTERRUPTED). Idempotent -- ``canceled: false``
with ``run_id: null`` when no gradual job is running for this
``(item, season)``. 404 only when the item itself doesn't exist.

#8 / #20 T2: library-wide metadata re-sync.

Dispatches EACH item through its RESOLVED-provider metadata refresh arm --
the SAME :func:`_refresh_metadata_arms` the per-item "Refresh & Scan" uses,
never re-derived: a ``tmdb`` item re-fetches its TMDB detail (backfilling the
NULL ``tvdb_id``/``imdb_id`` on pre-id-translation rows via
``apply_item_metadata``, never overwriting a stored id), a ``tvdb`` series
re-syncs via ``refresh_tvdb_series``, and a ``hybrid`` series re-assembles via
``assemble_hybrid_tree``. This closes the earlier TMDB-only gap where a
tvdb-only series (``tmdb_id`` NULL) was silently SKIPPED. Per-item failures
are isolated (rolled back + counted), never fatal.

The reused arms UPSERT titles/art, PRESERVE ``monitored``, and honour the
#111 numbering freeze (tvdb_tree.py / the hybrid sentinel) -- so a filed tree
is never renumbered or rebuilt here. Like the per-item refresh, an arm fires
the gated best-effort ``autorename_after_title_change`` when a real episode
title changes (the earlier TMDB-only path never renamed -- a deliberate
parity gain).

INVARIANT (arr-parity, #34) -- METADATA-ONLY BY DESIGN: this endpoint must
NEVER be extended to call ``rescan_item`` / force-reprobe library-wide. A
single action that force-re-analyses every file across a cold debrid mount is
the days-long re-sweep incident; a library-wide disk force must stay
impossible. ``_refresh_metadata_arms`` contains NO rescan/force-reprobe -- the
disk-scan tail lives only in ``_refresh_item_body``. If a whole-library disk
refresh is ever wanted, it must go through a scope cap (see
``bulk_routes.MAX_FORCE_REPROBE_ITEMS``), not here.

`original_file_path`) for existing files imported before those columns
existed, from grab history (`Download.release_title` -> GRABBED

rescore -- so files that scored 0 against their tokenless renamed on-disk name
(the Seinfeld defect) finally score their DTS-HD MA / DV / HDR custom formats.

second call returns 0. The `/api/v1` trigger for the standing "no code/DB-only
recovery path" rule. A literal segment, so it never collides with the
`{file_id:int}` PATCH route below.

`include_when_renaming` custom format each existing file's release matches --

touching `cf_score`. Adopts a pre-fix library where a renamable
streaming-service tag (ALL4, AMZN, iP, ...) the item's profile does not score

every "Refresh & Scan" (see `refresh_adopted_file_attrs`), so it is not
manual-only. A literal segment, so it never collides with `{file_id:int}`.

post.description:
LAYER 3 (edition tier routing): move a stray movie file onto a SIBLING
edition of the SAME item -- the self-serve version of the GTA recovery (a 1080p
file filed under the 4K edition, invisible behind the single `movie_file`
scalar). Relocates the on-disk file to the target edition's root and reattaches
it (`edition_id` + `relative_path`).

Data-safety: the relocation reuses the SAME verified, symlink-aware, abort-safe
mover as the edition root change (`repoint_movie_file` -> `_move_pairs`: STAGE
at the new root -> VERIFY present -> DELETE the old copy; a symlink is recreated
pointing at the same target, never a cross-filesystem hardlink) -- never a
hand-rolled rename/unlink. A move failure leaves every byte under the OLD root
and rolls the transaction back (500 + a `FILE_MOVE_FAILED` audit).

Guards: the target edition must be a MOVIE edition of `item_id` (else 404) and
must be EMPTY -- no current movie file (else 409; the user resolves the conflict
rather than a silent replace in v1). Tiers need not match (this is a manual fix
tool). Records a `RETARGETED` history row on the target edition + item. Returns
the updated target-edition view.

#91: delete MANY on-disk files (a "Manage episodes/files" multi-selection)
in ONE request, instead of the browser looping the per-file
``DELETE /files/{id}`` sequentially -- N HTTP round-trips, each doing a
(slow on a debrid/rclone mount) unlink + commit + a per-file arr webhook, so
a season was minutes of feedback-less waiting.

The heavy delete loop runs OFF the event loop; the route returns ``202
{run_id, total}`` immediately so the frontend polls ``/system/runs/{run_id}``
for live ``deleting`` progress (X of N) + a Stop-free but honest count, and on
completion reads the ``bulk_delete_summary`` (deleted vs failed). ``run_id`` is
``None`` (``total == 0``) when ``file_ids`` is empty.

Data-safety is IDENTICAL to the single-file path: each file is removed via the
SAME audited :func:`remove_media_file` in its OWN short transaction (audit +
``DELETED(MANUAL)`` history before delete, symlink-safe unlink, fileless slot →
Missing, owning imported Download retired, never a dangling-link prune), the
write lock is released between the slow unlinks, and the arr file-delete
webhook fires ONCE at the end (not per file). ``blocklist``/``search`` default
FALSE (a bulk delete is not a re-grab). Idempotent: an already-gone or
foreign file id is skipped, not fatal.

W5 + P3: remove a genuinely-unresolved file record ON PURPOSE (no re-grab).

W1's disk-reconcile deliberately NEVER prunes a present-but-unresolved link
(a transiently-evicted decypharr/zurg mount must not lose the file), and its
absence prune only fires on a manual Refresh & Scan -- so a permanently
DANGLING link or a flagged-ABSENT file (`missing_since`, the W1 window) can
sit as an un-healable zombie row that blocks its own re-grab. This gives the
user an explicit, deliberate cleanup: it removes the file and writes a
`DELETED`/`DISK_MISSING` audit via the SAME `remove_media_file` helper the
other delete surfaces use -- WITHOUT guessing permanence from a scan (the
user asserts it).

P3 widens the accepted set from dangling-only to BOTH unresolved states
(:func:`_file_removable_unresolved`). Guarded so it can never be mistaken for
a general delete: a file that is present/resolvable -- including one whose
`missing_since` flag is a stale lie after a recovery -- is a 422; the
healthy-file case must go through the normal `DELETE /files/{id}`.
`/files/{id}/cleanup-link` is a literal path, so it never collides with the
`{item_id:int}` routes.

Forget ONE unlinked file RECORD (audited). By DEFAULT the file on disk is
left completely alone -- only the DB row goes; `delete_from_disk=true` opts
into removing the file too (recycle-bin + symlink aware).

404 for an unknown id (never a 500 -- the UI's list is a 5s poll, so a row
may already be gone by the time it is clicked). 409 for a file that IS linked
to a title, and 409 when an opted-in disk delete cannot resolve an absolute
path (nothing is removed in either case).

Bulk sibling of :func:`forget_unlinked_media_file`, so a user with 16
orphan rows is not clicking 16 times.

Loops the EXPLICIT selection per file, committing each removal on its own; a
missing / linked / path-unresolvable row is reported as a per-file skip
rather than failing the batch (mirrors `_bulk_file_replace`). There is no
"everything matching unlinked" mode -- the ids the UI displays are the ids
that get removed, so its confirm count can never understate the damage.

Replace a genuinely-dead DANGLING file: delete it (audited) and dispatch
an edition-scoped monitored re-grab. Safety-critical guard (holes A/#3/E):
stands down with 409 (deleting NOTHING) on a live PRESENT (the stored flag
was stale -- cleared), an UNKNOWN/outage classification, or an ACTIVE
non-terminal ``Download`` on the slot. ``/files/{id}/replace`` is a literal
path, so it never collides with the ``{item_id:int}`` routes.

#90 ``?force=true`` (the one-confirm "Replace anyway"): NARROWLY permits a
present, byte-readable, MEDIAINFO-analysis-FAILED file (unparseable, not
dead) to be removed + re-grabbed. It never lets a healthy present file be
deleted and never bypasses the in-flight-download stand-down.

Bulk sibling of :func:`replace_media_file`: loops the selection per file
(per-file commit), applying the same guards. A per-file stand-down / missing
row is recorded rather than 409-ing the whole batch. #90 ``?force=true``
widens each per-file guard to the analysis-failed present case (same narrow
scope as the single route).

#82 dead-link "Search replacement" (one click): DELETE this edition's
genuinely-dead DANGLING files (audited) and dispatch an edition-scoped
monitored re-grab. Powers the dead-link attention banner -- a plain search
left the dead file in place (the edition still "had" a file), so the re-grab
could no-op; this deletes the dead link(s) first, then searches.

Reuses the per-file Replace guards via :func:`_bulk_file_replace`: only
LIVE-DANGLING files are removed (a stale flag / recovered file stands down,
deleting NOTHING; a live-present or actively-downloading slot is never nuked).
Selection is server-side (this edition's ``link_dangling`` files), so the UI
never has to enumerate file ids. Empty result when nothing is dangling (the
flag cleared between the banner render and the click).

P3(b): remove an unresolved file record (DANGLING or flagged-ABSENT,
:func:`_file_removable_unresolved`) and dispatch an edition-scoped monitored
re-grab -- the primary remedy for a truly-gone edition. Refuses a
present/recovered file with 422 (nothing removed). `/files/{id}/remove-and-
regrab` is a literal path, so it never collides with the `{item_id:int}`
routes.

get.description:
SEARCH-TRANSPARENCY B2: explain WHY this scope's AUTO-search is paused.

USER REPORT ("auto grabs nothing but interactive has many", #148 family):
three separate silencers pause auto-search with no surfaced reason -- the
per-(edition, season) BacklogBackoff backoff, the per-(edition, episode)
FailureCadence failed-grab cooldown, and a run of empty passes. Interactive
Search bypasses all three, so the modal listed many releases while auto sat
idle and unexplained. This surfaces all three signals plus the newest run's
outcome counts so the modal can render "auto paused until HH:MM".

DECLARED ``def`` (SYNC), NOT ``async``, ON PURPOSE: FastAPI runs a sync route
in its threadpool, so these four read-only SQLite queries execute OFF the
event loop automatically -- the same off-loop discipline the decypharr
poll-storm freeze fixes demand. Making this ``async`` would put the blocking
reads back on the loop and reintroduce the freeze; do NOT.

SEARCH-TRANSPARENCY B3: the currently-PAUSED auto-search slots for a whole
ITEM, in ONE read — so the detail page can chip each affected episode/season
without polling scope-status per row (that N+1 is the /attention perf class).

Returns ONLY active pauses (absence ⇒ not paused):
* failed-grab cooldown per (edition, episode) — CHEAP because the max window
  is the last ``failed_grab_cooldown_schedule_seconds`` entry (default 30 min),
  so only episodes with a ``DOWNLOAD_FAILED`` inside that window can be cooling
  down; that candidate set is tiny.
* empty-search backoff per (edition, season) — the active ``backlog_backoff``
  rows for the item's editions.

Sync ``def`` (like :func:`scope_status`) so the read-only queries run OFF the
event loop in FastAPI's threadpool — never re-introduce the decypharr freeze.

get.description:
#153: library-wide MediaInfo enrichment progress for the import landing
page. Counts are computed in SQL from the denormalized ``MediaFile`` columns
(a COUNT, never a per-file disk probe), so a poll stays cheap even on a large
library; the ``issues`` list is bounded (cap 50) with owning titles resolved.

light_read_guard: the UI polls this (and ``/sessions``) every ~5s during an
import, and under a big commit these COUNT/issue queries slow down; a
refetch storm (plus decypharr's arr poll) could otherwise pin the whole
connection pool on these reads and starve HTTP, freezing the app (the P1
incident). The guard caps how many such reads touch SQLite at once -- a
waiter parks a threadpool thread but holds no connection -- so the pool
always keeps headroom. These are SQL COUNTs over denormalized columns +
a bounded (<=50) issue list, so they take the WIDE light tier (connection
ceiling only). Sync-``def`` (off the event loop) so a stall can never block
the loop.

post.description:
Fire-then-poll commit. The 918-title cold-mount adopt took ~5.5 min INLINE
and hung the POST, so the actual adopt is BACKGROUNDED (mirrors ``start_scan``):
this route validates synchronously (so a bad root / missing profile / nothing
accepted still 400/404s here, better UX than a FAILED background job), flips
the session DRAFT -> COMMITTING + stamps the progress bar, commits so the row
is immediately pollable, then hands the id to ``app.state.import_commit_runner``
and returns 202 with the now-COMMITTING session. The report is no longer
returned here — the frontend polls ``GET /session/{id}`` (the bar while
COMMITTING, ``commit_result`` once COMMITTED).

Pause this import's enrichment task -- the sweep SKIPS its files until
resumed.

Resume a paused import enrichment task -- the sweep enriches its files
again.

Cancel this import's enrichment task -- the sweep permanently SKIPS its
files.

Dismiss this import's enrichment subtask from the task list -- HIDE-ONLY,
NON-DESTRUCTIVE. It sets a display flag and touches NOTHING else: the files
are untouched and the session's ``enrichment_control`` is unchanged (a
cancelled batch that can never finish is exactly what a user clears from
view).

Restore a dismissed enrichment subtask to the task list (the symmetric
inverse of dismiss). Equally NON-DESTRUCTIVE.

Put files back into the media-analysis backlog so the sweep re-probes them.

The repeatable companion to migration 0077's one-shot amnesty: it is how a
user recovers files that are blank in the UI because their import probe
failed (or was retired) under an older, tighter ffprobe bound -- raise the
``probe_timeout_seconds`` knob, then requeue.

Deliberately a pure DB RESET (clear the attempt counter, failure stamp and
reason) -- NO inline probing, so the request stays short and the patient
work happens in the background sweep that already owns it. Files whose
analysis can never succeed as configured ("unsupported"/"disabled") are not
requeued, and ``content_dead`` rows are left strictly alone: #141's
dead-content window is a SEPARATE state machine.

failure; ``all`` also picks up never-analysed files. ``media_file_ids``
narrows either scope to specific files.

clears the slot (→ heuristic fallback); a non-null one must reference an
existing quality profile / root folder (validated by the router → 404).

AddDefaultsUpdate.title: AddDefaultsUpdate
AddDefaultsUpdate.description:
Bulk upsert body for `PUT /api/v1/config/add-defaults`: each listed slot
is upserted; a slot's null FK clears that assignment. Slots omitted from the
list are left untouched.

AddLocalCredentialRequest.title: AddLocalCredentialRequest
AddLocalCredentialRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/{id}/credentials/local` -- add a password to a person.

Only the password is accepted; ``provider`` (``local``) and ``external_id``
(``lower(username)``) are ALWAYS server-derived (INV2) -- never read from the
body -- so a client can neither choose the credential's identity key nor point
it at another person. Creates the ``local`` credential where a Plex-first
person had none (add-a-password) and keeps ``users.password_hash`` in sync.

AnimeSettingsRead.title: AnimeSettingsRead
AnimeSettingsRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/settings/anime` -- the anime id-mapping config surface.

Kept OFF the main `/settings` DTO (precedent: the TRaSH anime-preference
toggles served by `PUT /trash/anime-preferences`), so the anime feature
area owns its own settings endpoint.

AnimeSettingsUpdate.title: AnimeSettingsUpdate
AnimeSettingsUpdate.description:
PUT payload for /api/v1/settings/anime. All fields optional -- only
supplied fields are written (mirrors `AppSettingsUpdate`).

AppApiKeyRead.title: AppApiKeyRead
AppApiKeyRead.description:
LF-B5: the ONE place the fusionha native app API key is returned by
value -- `GET /settings/api-key` (reveal) and
`POST /settings/regenerate-api-key` (rotate).

AppSettingsRead.description:
Effective app-settings values, secrets redacted.

Mirrors `fusionha.services.settings.SETTINGS_REGISTRY` minus the
sensitive `tmdb_api_key` value itself, which is only ever exposed as
`tmdb_configured: bool` (per `SENSITIVE_KEYS`).

AppSettingsUpdate.title: AppSettingsUpdate
AppSettingsUpdate.description:
PUT payload for /api/v1/settings.

All fields optional -- only supplied fields are written. `extra="forbid"`
makes an unknown top-level key a 422 at the validation layer. `tmdb_api_key`
is secret-preserving: omitted or a blank/whitespace-only value leaves the
stored secret unchanged (see settings_routes.update_app_settings), so a PUT
that round-trips a redacted GET body (which never carries the raw key)
can never wipe it.

ApproveEditionSpec.title: ApproveEditionSpec
ApproveEditionSpec.description:
One edition to enable when approving a request (the approve dialog's
edition picker — the shared EditionConfig). `root_folder_id`/
`quality_profile_id` are OPTIONAL: omitted, they fall to the Add-defaults
matrix for this `(kind, tier)` (same as a plain approve). `movie_edition`
composes with the tier so a Director's Cut can be enabled alongside the
default.

ApproveRequest.title: ApproveRequest
ApproveRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/requests/{id}/approve` — OPTIONAL body. `editions` is the
admin's selection from the approve dialog; omitted (the plain approve), the
request's requested tier is enabled as before. The requested tier is always
ensured regardless. `search` kicks a search for the enabled editions.

ArrConnectionCreate.title: ArrConnectionCreate
ArrConnectionCreate.description:
`POST /arr-connections`: a saved connection to a live Sonarr/Radarr the
preset capture flow reads profiles from.

ArrConnectionRead.title: ArrConnectionRead
ArrConnectionRead.description:
An arr connection with its secret redacted: `api_key` is never
serialized; `api_key_configured` says whether one is stored.

ArrConnectionTestResult.title: ArrConnectionTestResult
ArrConnectionTestResult.description:
`POST /arr-connections/{id}/test`: reachability of the arr's
`/api/v3/system/status` (with the stored X-Api-Key) + detected version.

ArrConnectionUpdate.title: ArrConnectionUpdate
ArrConnectionUpdate.description:
`PUT /arr-connections/{id}`. A `None`/blank `api_key` leaves the stored
key untouched (write-only secret semantics, like SearchIndexer).

ArrCustomFormatImportRequest.title: ArrCustomFormatImportRequest

ArrWebhookCreate.title: ArrWebhookCreate
ArrWebhookCreate.description:
`instance_id` picks the virtual instance the connection is scoped to
-- required on create, fixed thereafter (an update can't move a
registration between instances).

ArrWebhookGroup.title: ArrWebhookGroup
ArrWebhookGroup.description: arr-registered webhooks grouped by the virtual instance they live on.

ArrWebhookPathMapping.title: ArrWebhookPathMapping
ArrWebhookPathMapping.description:
PR 2 of the arr Connect Notification feature: one `from` -> `to`
prefix rewrite applied to every PATH field a webhook emits. Longest
matching `from` wins when several are configured; see
`arrapi.notifications.map_path`.

ArrWebhookRead.title: ArrWebhookRead
ArrWebhookRead.description:
One arr-registered notification connection (an ``ArrNotification`` row),
as surfaced in Settings -> Connect. `source` == "decypharr"/"overseerr"
marks a registration an external tool owns (display + delete only there);
a fusionha-created one is user-editable via the write routes below. The
target ``url`` is shown (it identifies the connection), but any auth secret
the webhook carries (a WebhookSettings ``password``) is redacted to a bool.

BackfillRenamingFormatsResponse.title: BackfillRenamingFormatsResponse
BackfillRenamingFormatsResponse.description:
`POST /api/v1/library/files/backfill-renaming-formats` (#100) -- how many
existing files gained an `include_when_renaming` custom-format tag (ALL4,
AMZN, iP, ...) that their profile does not score, added ADD-ONLY to
`custom_formats` without touching `cf_score`. Idempotent: a second call
returns 0.

BackfillSceneNamesResponse.title: BackfillSceneNamesResponse
BackfillSceneNamesResponse.description:
`POST /api/v1/library/files/backfill-scene-names` (Task F) -- how many
existing files had their preserved release name (`scene_name` /
`original_file_path`) recovered from grab history + rescored. Idempotent: a
second call returns 0.

BacklogSearchCancel.title: BacklogSearchCancel
BacklogSearchCancel.description:
The body of the backlog-sweep Stop endpoint (deliverable C), mirroring
``GradualSeasonSearchCancel``. ``canceled`` is True when a live sweep was
found + flagged to stop (before its next target); ``run_id`` echoes that run
(``None`` when no sweep was running for the id -- idempotent).

BackupConfigUpdate.title: BackupConfigUpdate
BackupConfigUpdate.description: Partial update of the scheduled-backup config (all optional).

BackupRecordRead.title: BackupRecordRead
BackupRecordRead.description: One backup archive on disk (list/download rows).

BlocklistClearResult.title: BlocklistClearResult
BlocklistClearResult.description: Result of ``DELETE /blocklist/all`` -- how many entries were cleared.

BlocklistCreateRequest.title: BlocklistCreateRequest
BlocklistCreateRequest.description:
MANUALLY blocklist a release (arr's "Blocklist" / "Blocklist and search").

The release is identified by ONE of:

* ``history_id`` -- a ``History`` primary key (the ``id`` in
  ``GET /api/v1/history`` and ``ItemDetailRead.history``). The primary path:
  it works long after the download left the queue.
* ``download_id`` -- a ``Download`` PRIMARY KEY (the ``id`` in ``QueueRead``
  / ``DELETE /api/v1/queue/{id}``). NOT ``History.download_id``, which is
  the download client's own opaque job id.

BulkDeleteResultRead.title: BulkDeleteResultRead
BulkDeleteResultRead.description:
#91: the outcome of a completed bulk file delete, retained on the
run-capture summary channel and surfaced as
``CommandRunDetailRead.bulk_delete_summary`` once the run goes terminal.
``requested`` is how many file ids the request carried (post de-dup);
``deleted`` + ``failed`` are the removed vs errored counts (a skipped
already-gone id counts as neither).

BulkEpisodeAssign.title: BulkEpisodeAssign
BulkEpisodeAssign.description:
Episode/season (re)assignment for the bulk editor. All `episode_ids` must
belong to `season` of the item. An empty `episode_ids` REASSIGNS each
selected file to the same episode NUMBER in `season` (the "Select Season"
action for files that span seasons); a non-empty list assigns the selected
file(s) to those episode(s) -- one episode applied to all, or a 1:1 pairing
when the count matches the number of selected files.

BulkFileDeleteRequest.title: BulkFileDeleteRequest
BulkFileDeleteRequest.description:
#91: the body of ``POST /library/{item_id}/files/bulk-delete``. Deletes
every ``MediaFile`` in ``file_ids`` in ONE request. ``blocklist``/``search``
default FALSE -- a bulk delete is a delete, not a re-grab; set ``search`` to
dispatch the same guarded replacement search the single-file path uses per
freed slot (and ``blocklist`` to additionally ban each removed file's owning
release).

BulkFileDeleteStart.title: BulkFileDeleteStart
BulkFileDeleteStart.description:
#91: the 202 body of ``POST /library/{item_id}/files/bulk-delete``.

``run_id`` is the opened ``CommandRun`` the frontend polls
(``/system/runs/{run_id}``) for live ``deleting`` progress (X of N) and, once
terminal, the ``bulk_delete_summary``; ``None`` when there was nothing to
delete (``total == 0``, no background job spawned). ``total`` is the number of
(de-duplicated) file ids the delete will attempt.

BulkFileEditRequest.title: BulkFileEditRequest
BulkFileEditRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/v1/library/{id}/files/bulk-edit` -- the Manage-Episodes
bulk SET/override. `file_ids` selects the files (all must belong to the
item). Every attribute is OPTIONAL and only applied when the key is present
(partial `PATCH` semantics via `model_fields_set`):

* `quality` overrides the parsed quality (a `QualityName` from the quality
  definitions; `null` is ignored -- quality is never cleared).
* `release_group` is free text applied VERBATIM; an empty string / `null`
  CLEARS it.
* `languages` / `indexer_flags` REPLACE the file's set (an empty list
  clears); validated against the canonical `Language` / `IndexerFlag` enums.
* `release_type` overrides the `ReleaseType`.
* `proper` / `real` set the arr revision (#95/#109): `proper` bumps the
  file's `proper_version` (True -> 1, False -> 0), `real` flags a REAL
  re-release. Both feed the Proper/Repack + Real custom-format scoring; a
  `null` is a no-op.
* `episodes` (re)assigns the selected file(s) to episode(s)/a season.

After any change every touched file's CF score is re-derived. `extra="forbid"`
(unknown field -> 422) matches the sibling request DTOs.

BulkRefreshRequest.title: BulkRefreshRequest
BulkRefreshRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/v1/library/bulk/refresh`: open a Refresh & Scan run per
listed item and dispatch each as a background task (the same #150 concurrency
gate a single per-item refresh queues on). `metadata_only` mirrors the
per-item `?metadata_only` flag -- skip the disk rescan, refresh TMDB metadata
only.

BulkRefreshResult.title: BulkRefreshResult
BulkRefreshResult.description:
Result of `POST /api/v1/library/bulk/refresh`. `runs` = the opened
(item_id, run_id) pairs, one per resolved item; `errors` = the count of
requested `item_ids` that were not found / skipped (never a 500).

BulkRefreshRun.title: BulkRefreshRun
BulkRefreshRun.description:
One opened Refresh & Scan run in a bulk-refresh response -- the item it
covers and the `CommandRun` id the frontend can poll `/system/runs/{run_id}`
for live progress.

BulkReplaceItem.title: BulkReplaceItem
BulkReplaceItem.description:
One file's outcome in a bulk Replace. A guard stand-down / missing row is
recorded (``deleted=False`` + ``reason``) rather than failing the batch.

BulkReplaceRequest.title: BulkReplaceRequest
BulkReplaceRequest.description: Body for `POST /library/files/replace` (bulk): the selected file ids.

BulkReplaceResponse.title: BulkReplaceResponse
BulkReplaceResponse.description:
Aggregate of a bulk Replace: per-file outcomes plus the monitored /
unmonitored partition counts (both partitions may search -- the split is
informational, distinct from the auto path that drops unmonitored slots).

BulkRootError.title: BulkRootError
BulkRootError.description:
A single per-edition failure/skip in a tier-scoped bulk root move.

Distinct from `BulkTargetError` (a bare `{id, error}`): a bulk root move
reports the offending *edition* and the *item* it belongs to so the UI can
point at the exact title + tier row that failed (an item that lacks the tier
is skipped-and-counted separately, not reported here).

BulkRootResult.title: BulkRootResult

BulkSetMinimumAvailabilityRequest.title: BulkSetMinimumAvailabilityRequest
BulkSetMinimumAvailabilityRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/v1/library/bulk/minimum-availability`: bulk-set the
Radarr per-movie minimum availability on the selected targets' MOVIE
editions. `minimum_availability` is validated as a `MinimumAvailability`
wire value (announced|inCinemas|released; anything else -> 422). Series
editions in the selection are left untouched (their column stays NULL);
`affected` counts only the movie editions actually updated.

ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest
ChangePasswordRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/{id}/change-password` (CA-1).

A NON-admin self-service change verifies `current_password` against the
target before storing the new hash. A PRIVILEGED caller (admin / app-key /
auth-off) may RESET any account's password without knowing the current one,
so `current_password` is optional (ignored on the privileged path).

CheckFourKResult.title: CheckFourKResult
CheckFourKResult.description:
Result of the on-demand ``POST /api/v1/library/{item_id}/check-4k`` probe
(#62 Phase 3). ``dispatched`` is False when real integrations are off (nothing
was queried). ``queried_indexers`` is how many indexers this explicit action
spent a query against; ``found_uhd`` / ``seasons_seen`` / ``best_release_name``
reflect the genuine (non-upscale) 2160p availability recorded for the item
after the probe.

CollectionAddRequest.title: CollectionAddRequest
CollectionAddRequest.description:
Batch-add the missing films of a collection. `tmdb_ids` are the films the
user chose to add (owned ones are AUTO-SKIPPED server-side and any id not in
the collection is dropped); `editions` is ONE shared edition config (HD-1080p
default + optional UHD-4K), applied to EVERY film added. `monitor` /
`minimum_availability` / `search_on_add` mirror the single-title add.

CollectionAddResultRead.title: CollectionAddResultRead
CollectionAddResultRead.description:
The outcome of a batch collection add. `added` are the freshly-created
items; `skipped_owned` the requested ids already in the library (never
re-added); `library_item_ids` the ids of everything added; `failed` the ids
whose per-film add raised (partial success -- the loop keeps going).

CollectionDetailRead.title: CollectionDetailRead
CollectionDetailRead.description:
The full film list of a collection + per-part ownership -- serves both the
detail Collection tab and the Add-collection modal's source.

CollectionPartRead.title: CollectionPartRead
CollectionPartRead.description:
One film in a collection + the user's ownership of it (detail tab grid +
Add-modal film list). THREE-STATE: `owned` is the library `in_library`
identity (a MOVIE item exists); `has_file` is whether that item has a present
file on disk. So the badge is: not `owned` -> add (not in fusionha); `owned`
+ `has_file` -> green check (file on disk); `owned` + not `has_file` -> amber
caution (tracked, no file yet). `tiers` are its owned quality tiers.

CollectionRefRead.title: CollectionRefRead
CollectionRefRead.description:
The DB-only collection reference stamped on a movie's detail read (so the
frontend can gate the Collection tab on `item.collection` without a live
TMDB call). The tab then fetches the films lazily via
`GET /api/v1/collections/{collection_tmdb_id}`.

CollectionSummaryRead.title: CollectionSummaryRead
CollectionSummaryRead.description:
One rail card: a partially-owned franchise + its completion fraction
(`owned_count`/`total_count`). Only INCOMPLETE, partially-owned collections
are surfaced by `GET /api/v1/collections` (ranked closest-to-done).

CommandRead.title: CommandRead
CommandRead.description:
ST-B1: one command -- an execution instance of a task
(``GET /api/v1/system/commands`` and the ``POST .../run`` response).

``status`` is ``running`` while in flight, then ``completed`` or ``failed``;
``message`` carries the failure reason (``None`` otherwise); ``progress`` is
an optional 0..1 fraction for long jobs.

CommandRunDetailRead.title: CommandRunDetailRead
CommandRunDetailRead.description:
A single run PLUS its full `RunCandidate` decision trail (grouped-friendly:
each candidate carries its own `action`, so the UI can bucket the trail into
grabbed/upgraded/rejected/skipped sections).

CommandRunRead.title: CommandRunRead
CommandRunRead.description:
One decision-making pass (the Recent+Running feed row).

Carries the structured counts (releases/evaluated/grabbed/upgraded/rejected/
errors) and the denormalised target descriptor (item_id/media_kind/scope/
target_title) so the frontend voice is title-aware even after the item is
deleted. `status` is `running` while in flight, then `completed`/`failed`/
`interrupted` (a restart reconciles orphans).

CommandStatus.title: CommandStatus

CommandTrigger.title: CommandTrigger
CommandTrigger.description:
What kicked off a :class:`~fusionha.models.command_run.CommandRun`.

The task-run + decision-trail feature records every decision-making pass
(RSS sync, scheduled sync, search-on-add, a manual/interactive search) so
the Recent feed can narrate what fusionha did and why. Values are stable
wire tokens the API/UI filter on.

CredentialRead.title: CredentialRead
CredentialRead.description:
One sign-in method a user (person) owns -- linked-identity Phase 1.

The read-side projection of a :class:`~fusionha.models.credentials.UserCredential`.
The stored ``secret`` (the local password hash) is NEVER serialized -- exactly
like ``UserRead`` carries no password. ``external_id`` is the server-derived
login key (``lower(username)`` for local, ``str(plex id)`` for plex) and is
surfaced only as a display aid; it is never accepted from a client on write.

CredentialUpdate.title: CredentialUpdate
CredentialUpdate.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}/credentials/{cid}` -- set primary / (de)activate.

Both fields optional. ``is_primary=True`` reconciles the person to exactly one
primary (others demoted). ``is_active=False`` disables the credential at login
(fails closed) and revokes the identity's live sessions; it is refused when it
would leave the person with zero active credentials (INV7). ``provider`` /
``external_id`` / ``secret`` are NOT settable here (INV2).

DeadSlotHint.title: DeadSlotHint
DeadSlotHint.description:
decypharr's `release_dead` push (post-import dead articles).

A HINT only: it schedules ONE debounced on-demand import-poll pass, and that
pass re-reads the failed slot from decypharr itself. Nothing in this body is
acted on directly -- it is validated and logged, never trusted as data (an
attacker holding a valid key still cannot name a release to delete).

DeadSlotHintResult.title: DeadSlotHintResult
DeadSlotHintResult.description:
Whether the hint actually scheduled a pass (`False` when debounced, or
when `post_import_dead_callback_enabled` is off). Always HTTP 202.

DeleteLooseFileRequest.title: DeleteLooseFileRequest
DeleteLooseFileRequest.description:
#62: body for `POST /api/v1/library/{id}/manage-files/delete` -- delete ONE
loose (unregistered) on-disk video under the item's root(s) BY PATH (a loose
file has no `MediaFile` row to address by id).

`path` is REQUIRED and must be a genuine loose file under this item -- the
route validates it against `loose_files(item)` before touching disk, so an
arbitrary/traversal path is rejected 422. `extra="forbid"` (unknown field ->
422) matches the sibling request DTOs.

DemoConfigUpdate.title: DemoConfigUpdate
DemoConfigUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/v1/demo` -- configure the demo. Every field optional; an omitted
field keeps its stored value. `demo_password` is WRITE-ONLY (hashed on set,
never echoed); setting it — or the username / require-credentials — rotates
the demo access token so live demo cookies die.

DemoCounts.title: DemoCounts
DemoCounts.description:
Cheap server-computed sample-library tallies for the demo config UI's
count strip. All derived from bounded aggregate COUNT queries (no per-row
loads) so the UI never re-derives them.

DemoLoginRequest.title: DemoLoginRequest
DemoLoginRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/demo/login` -- a visitor entering the read-only demo. When
`demo_require_credentials` is on, the username/password must match the
admin-set demo credentials; when off, any (or empty) body is accepted.

DemoSeedResult.title: DemoSeedResult
DemoSeedResult.description:
Result of a demo seed/reset/wipe. ``seeded`` (how many sample items now
exist) is kept for back-compat; the added fields report the alive-state rows
the op produced (seed/reset) or the item rows it removed (wipe).

DemoStatusRead.title: DemoStatusRead
DemoStatusRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/demo` -- the public read-only showcase's current state. The
demo password is NEVER returned — only `demo_password_set` (whether one
exists), so the editor can prompt to set/rotate it.

DisconnectRequest.title: DisconnectRequest
DisconnectRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/credentials/disconnect` -- remove a whole provider
across all identities. `fallback` decides the fate of an identity left with no
sign-in method (`disable`/`delete`/`password`-refuse). `dry_run` (default True)
previews the affected identities without mutating.

DiscoverCheckFourKRequest.title: DiscoverCheckFourKRequest
DiscoverCheckFourKRequest.description:
#71 DISCOVER PRE-ADD CHECK body: probe a not-yet-added Discover title for
genuine 2160p availability. Carries the TMDB metadata the Discover card
already holds -- no ``MediaItem`` exists yet, so nothing is looked up or
persisted. ``tmdb_id`` gives releases an id match; ``title`` + ``year`` drive
the query + fuzzy match; ``kind`` picks movie vs series parsing.

DiscoverCheckFourKResult.title: DiscoverCheckFourKResult
DiscoverCheckFourKResult.description:
#71 result -- the same shape as :class:`CheckFourKResult` minus ``item_id``
(there is no item), so the frontend renders the verdict + CF chips
identically to the Add-edition modal's check.

DiscoverIgnoreCreate.title: DiscoverIgnoreCreate
DiscoverIgnoreCreate.description:
Create a Discover ignore. `scope="collection"` ignores the whole
collection (`tmdb_id` omitted); `scope="item"` ignores `tmdb_id` within
`collection_tmdb_id`. `name` is the display label (film title / collection
name); `collection_name` is the parent name for an item row.

DiscoverIgnoreRead.title: DiscoverIgnoreRead

DiscoverSort.title: DiscoverSort
DiscoverSort.description:
DV-B2: the filtered-Discover sort control. Maps to a TMDB `sort_by`
value per kind in `metadata.tmdb._SORT_BY`.

DiscoverWindow.title: DiscoverWindow
DiscoverWindow.description: DV-B1: the trending window toggle (Today / This Week).

DuplicateGroup.title: DuplicateGroup
DuplicateGroup.description:
A set of accounts a READ-ONLY heuristic flags as likely the same person --
same case-insensitive email, the `(plex:<id>)` twin of a bare local name, or
an identical normalised handle. NEVER auto-linked; an admin decides.

DuplicateMember.title: DuplicateMember
DuplicateMember.description: One account inside a likely-duplicate group (`GET /users/duplicates`).

EditionAddRequest.title: EditionAddRequest
EditionAddRequest.description:
EDITION-ADD: `POST /api/v1/library/{item_id}/editions` body -- add ONE
new quality edition to an ALREADY-added title (e.g. a 4K edition beside an
existing HD one, or a Director's Cut beside a Theatrical). Mirrors the
per-edition config `EditionCreate` carries on the native add, plus a
`search_now` grab trigger and a movie `minimum_availability`.

`movie_edition` composes with `tier` as the unique `(tier, movie_edition)`
key -- a movie cut (Director's Cut / ...) or, on a series (#115), the
"version" (Colour / Black & White). Accepted on either kind.
`monitor` is the per-edition SERIES monitor level (inert for a movie); when
omitted the edition takes the model default (`all`). `minimum_availability`
is the Radarr per-movie grab gate (inert for a series). `search_now=true`
fires a best-effort per-edition search right after the edition is created.
`extra="forbid"` matches the sibling edition/monitor request DTOs.

EditionReorderRequest.title: EditionReorderRequest
EditionReorderRequest.description:
Set every edition's `sort_order` in one call: the definition whose id is
at index `i` in `ids` gets `sort_order = i`. Any id absent from the DB is a
404 (the whole reorder is rejected rather than partially applied).

EditionUpdate.title: EditionUpdate
EditionUpdate.description:
MON-B1 + TRACK-B (#33): `PATCH /api/v1/library/{item_id}/editions/
{edition_id}` body -- edit one edition's MANAGEMENT fields. Partial +
`extra="forbid"`: only the supplied keys are written
(`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` in the route), matching the sibling
season/episode monitor toggles.

`monitored` is the on/off switch; `monitor` is the per-edition SERIES
monitor level (inert for a movie edition) and, when set, re-derives the
episode display union (`apply_series_monitor`). `quality_profile_id` /
`root_folder_id` retune this edition's profile + storage root (the route
422s an id that doesn't resolve); `minimum_availability` is the Radarr
per-movie grab gate (inert for a series edition), stored as its arr wire
string -- an explicit `null` clears it (falls back to "released").

`movie_edition` (#120/#115) composes with `tier` as the unique
`(tier, movie_edition)` key: on a movie it is the cut (Director's Cut /
Extended / ...) -- the "Edit Movie File" dialog's Edition field; on a series
it is the "version" (Colour / Black & White), labelled "Version" in the UI.
An explicit `null` clears it to the Standard/default; the route 409s a
change that would duplicate a `(tier, movie_edition)` already tracked on the
item (either kind).

EnrichmentControl.title: EnrichmentControl
EnrichmentControl.description:
User control state of a session's post-import enrichment task (#153).
