The import landing page shows a POST-IMPORT task scoped to a recent import
session's files (Enriching N of M for the files just imported); that task is
pausable/cancellable/resumable and must survive restarts, so its control state
is persisted on the durable :class:`~fusionha.models.import_session.ImportSession`:

* ``ACTIVE``    -- the durable sweep enriches this session's files normally;
* ``PAUSED``    -- the user paused the task; the sweep SKIPS this session's
  files (resumable -> ``ACTIVE``);
* ``CANCELLED`` -- the user cancelled the task; the sweep permanently SKIPS
  this session's files.

Lowercase wire values, ``native_enum=False`` (mirrors ``ImportSessionStatus``).

EnrichmentIssueRead.title: EnrichmentIssueRead
EnrichmentIssueRead.description:
One media file stuck without usable MediaInfo enrichment (#153). `reason`
is ``unreadable`` for a #141 content-dead file (its source is gone),
``unlinked`` for a file record attached to no title at all (``edition_id``
NULL and no ``episode_files`` row -- the item-scoped enrichment sweep can
never reach it, so it is a data-integrity issue to repair, never auto-pruned),
or ``probe_failed`` for a file whose probe attempts are exhausted
(``probe_attempts >= PROBE_FAIL_MAX``). `title` falls back to the file's own
name when no owning item resolves.

EnrichmentRequeueRequest.title: EnrichmentRequeueRequest
EnrichmentRequeueRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/import/enrichment/requeue`: put files back in the
media-analysis backlog so the sweep re-probes them.

The recovery action for files left blank by a probe that failed (or was
retired) under an older, tighter ffprobe bound -- raise
``probe_timeout_seconds`` in Media Management, then requeue.

EnrichmentRequeueResponse.title: EnrichmentRequeueResponse
EnrichmentRequeueResponse.description:
How many files were put back into the analysis backlog. The probing
itself happens in the background sweep -- this call never probes inline.

EnrichmentStatusRead.title: EnrichmentStatusRead
EnrichmentStatusRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/import/enrichment-status`: library-wide MediaInfo enrichment
progress, computed purely from the denormalized MediaFile columns (a COUNT,
never a per-file disk probe). `issues` is bounded (cap 50, ordered by id).
`subtasks` nests the per-import tasks (one per not-yet-complete committed
session) under this global task.

EpisodeDownloadState.title: EpisodeDownloadState
EpisodeDownloadState.description:
#105: one edition's LIVE download state on one episode.

Derived from in-flight `Download` rows keyed by (edition_id, episode_id),
mirroring the calendar's "grabbing" definition (`services.imports.
_NON_TERMINAL`) rather than a download-client poll: "downloading" (a
non-terminal Download for exactly this edition+episode is in flight and no
file is owned yet), "upgrading" (#152: that grab's episode ALREADY has a file
for this edition -- e.g. a season pack covering an episode that is already
imported -- so it is a better-copy upgrade, not a fresh fetch), or "stuck"
(that Download is in an error/warning state). Carried alongside -- NOT inside
-- `EpisodeRead.files`: a downloading episode has no file for the edition yet,
while an upgrading one does, so the per-episode status cell can show the grab.

EpisodeFileBulkDeletePayload.title: EpisodeFileBulkDeletePayload
EpisodeFileBulkDeletePayload.description:
Sonarr v3 `DELETE /episodefile/bulk` body — the episode-file (MediaFile)
ids to delete (decypharr blocking, series side).

EpisodeFileRead.title: EpisodeFileRead
EpisodeFileRead.description: One episode's file for a specific edition (the EpisodeFile link).

EpisodeFileResource.title: EpisodeFileResource
EpisodeFileResource.description:
Sonarr v3 `GET /episodefile` list item (#47a). Same faithful-subset
approach as MovieFileResource; `series_id` is the owning edition's id
(editions ARE the virtual-instance series rows).

EpisodeRef.title: EpisodeRef
EpisodeRef.description: One specific episode a series request scopes to (P2a): `{season, episode}`.

EpisodeResource.title: EpisodeResource
EpisodeResource.description:
Sonarr v3 episode record as paged by `GET /wanted/missing` (#58).
Faithful subset: `series_id` is the owning edition's id (editions ARE the
virtual-instance series rows), `series` is embedded so a consumer that
skips the extra `GET /series/{id}` still resolves the title.

FileReplaceResponse.title: FileReplaceResponse
FileReplaceResponse.description:
`POST /library/files/{id}/replace` result: the file was DANGLING, was
deleted (audited) and an edition-scoped search was dispatched.

FileRepointRequest.title: FileRepointRequest
FileRepointRequest.description:
LAYER 3 (edition tier routing): `POST /api/v1/library/{item_id}/files/
{file_id}/repoint` body -- move a stray movie file onto a SIBLING edition of
the same item (the self-serve GTA recovery). `edition_id` is the TARGET
edition; the route 404s an edition that is not a movie edition of this item and
409s a target that already has a movie file.

ForgetUnlinkedBulkRequest.title: ForgetUnlinkedBulkRequest
ForgetUnlinkedBulkRequest.description:
Body for `POST /library/files/forget-unlinked` (bulk). The ids are
REQUIRED and non-empty on purpose: there is no server-side "delete everything
matching unlinked" mode, so the count in the UI's confirm is exactly what gets
deleted -- a blanket predicate delete is how libraries get eaten.

ForgetUnlinkedRequest.title: ForgetUnlinkedRequest
ForgetUnlinkedRequest.description:
Body for `POST /library/files/{id}/forget-unlinked`. `extra="forbid"`
(unknown field -> 422) matches the sibling command bodies -- a misspelled
`deleteFromDisk` must never be silently read as "leave the file alone" OR as
an opt-in.

ForgetUnlinkedResponse.title: ForgetUnlinkedResponse
ForgetUnlinkedResponse.description:
Aggregate of a bulk forget: how many records went, plus a per-file skip
list rather than a failed batch (mirrors `BulkReplaceResponse`).

ForgetUnlinkedSkip.title: ForgetUnlinkedSkip
ForgetUnlinkedSkip.description:
One file the bulk forget did NOT remove. `reason` is `not_found` (the row
is already gone), `linked` (it belongs to a title -- refused),
`path_unresolved` (`delete_from_disk` was asked for but the absolute path is
not derivable, so nothing was touched) or `disk_error` (the file removal
itself failed -- e.g. a read-only or vanished mount; that row is rolled back
and the rest of the batch continues).

FormatTagRead.title: FormatTagRead
FormatTagRead.description:
#62 card v2: one best-per-dimension CF chip. ``kind`` colour-codes it:
quality | hdr | audio | group.

FourKAvailableItem.title: FourKAvailableItem
FourKAvailableItem.description:
One HD-owned title for which a genuine (non-upscale) 2160p release has
been OBSERVED on indexers (#62 "4K Available" tab, Phase 1).

``hd_edition_id`` is the monitored HD·1080p edition that owns file(s) -- the
anchor a future "Add 4K edition" action (Phase 4) graduates from. Item-level
``best_*`` / ``seen_count`` / ``*_seen_at`` aggregate across the title's
availability rows; ``seasons`` carries the per-season detail for a series.

FourKAvailablePage.title: FourKAvailablePage

FourKSeasonAvailability.title: FourKSeasonAvailability
FourKSeasonAvailability.description:
One SERIES season for which a genuine 2160p release was observed (#62).
A movie / whole-item scope carries no season rows.

GradualSeasonSearchCancel.title: GradualSeasonSearchCancel
GradualSeasonSearchCancel.description:
#91: the body of the gradual season-search cancel endpoint. ``canceled``
is True when an in-flight job was found and flagged to stop (before its next
episode); ``run_id`` is that job's run (``None`` when no job was running).

GradualSeasonSearchStart.title: GradualSeasonSearchStart
GradualSeasonSearchStart.description:
#91: the body of ``POST /library/{id}/search/season/{season}/gradual``.

``run_id`` is the opened ``CommandRun`` the frontend polls
(``/system/runs/{run_id}``) for live per-episode progress + a Stop; ``None``
when there was nothing to search (``total == 0``, no background job spawned).
``total`` is the number of missing+monitored episodes queued this pass.
``already_running`` is True when a gradual job for this (item, season) was
already in flight -- the returned ``run_id``/``total`` then describe THAT
in-flight job (idempotent attach, not a second job).

HealthCheckRead.title: HealthCheckRead
HealthCheckRead.description:
One `HealthService` finding. Mirrors `arrapi.schemas.HealthCheckResource`
(the arr-facing v3 shape) but with fusionha's own snake_case naming.

HealthCheckResource.title: HealthCheckResource
HealthCheckResource.description: v3 `GET /health` list-item shape: `{source, type, message, wikiUrl?}`.

HeldDetailRead.title: HeldDetailRead
HeldDetailRead.description:
MANUAL-IMPORT-HOLD "why it's held": the structured comparison behind a
not-an-upgrade hold (``Download.held_detail``), so the queue UI can show the
EXACT reason and let the user decide (force-import / blocklist / delete).
Mirrors ``imports.build_not_an_upgrade_detail``'s dict 1:1. All fields are
display-only; NULL for a pre-feature / non-structured hold.

HeldResolutionRead.title: HeldResolutionRead
HeldResolutionRead.description: Probed frame geometry for a not-an-upgrade hold detail.

HistoryChip.title: HistoryChip
HistoryChip.description:
One parser-derived chip on a History "Stories" card header.

``kind`` is one of group / edition / source / range / audio / protocol;
``label`` is the human display text. Built by
:func:`fusionha.services.history_chips.build_history_chips`.

HistorySparklineDay.title: HistorySparklineDay
HistorySparklineDay.description:
One bucket of `GET /api/v1/history/sparkline` -- a REAL per-day event
count (``HistoryService.daily_counts``), replacing the old client-side
sparkline that only ever summed the loaded, recent-first page of rows (so
it degenerated into one tall "today" bar). Always ``days``-many of these,
oldest -> newest, zero-filled for a day with no events.

ImportScanRequest.title: ImportScanRequest
ImportScanRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/import/scan` body.

`default_profile_per_tier` is UI-advisory only (pre-fills the review grid);
it does not affect the scan and is not persisted -- `POST /import/commit`
carries the authoritative per-edition `quality_profile_id`.

ImportScanRootRequest.title: ImportScanRootRequest
ImportScanRootRequest.description:
One root to scan, with the tier AND kind the user assigned it.

`RootFolder` carries no tier/kind column (see the design's "Tier source"),
so both are supplied per run: tier drives the cross-root edition merge,
kind selects movie-vs-series TMDB lookups + file mapping. `kind` is a
fusionha addition to the spec's `{root_folder_id, tier}` body because the
scan genuinely needs it to look a folder up as a movie vs a series.

ImportSessionCreateRequest.title: ImportSessionCreateRequest
ImportSessionCreateRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/import/session` body -- the roots to open a triage session
over. One child scan is created (and kicked) per root, mirroring the legacy
`POST /import/scan` body but persisted under a resumable session.

ImportSessionDecisionPatch.title: ImportSessionDecisionPatch
ImportSessionDecisionPatch.description:
One upsert into a child scan's `decisions`, keyed by `(scan_id,
folder_key)`. Every intent field is OPTIONAL with partial-PATCH semantics
(only keys PRESENT in the body are applied, via `model_fields_set`): an
explicit `null` on `quality_profile_id`/`variant` CLEARS it, an omitted key
leaves it untouched. Applying any patch re-stamps the row's seen baseline to
the current match (acknowledging a `changed_since_reviewed` flag).

ImportSessionDecisionsPatchRequest.title: ImportSessionDecisionsPatchRequest
ImportSessionDecisionsPatchRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/import/session/{id}/decisions` body. The frontend debounces
every toggle into this; Accept-all-N is one PATCH of N patches. A patch
targeting a scan that is mid-rescan (`scanning`) 409s so an in-flight
auto-save can't clobber the merge.

ImportSessionItemRead.title: ImportSessionItemRead
ImportSessionItemRead.description:
One proposed title with the child scan's decision layer applied.

Extends the scan item read with `scan_id` + the stable `folder_key` (the
PATCH key) and the per-row decision fields resolved from `decisions`
(defaulted when the user hasn't touched the row yet). `variant` is the
user's cut OVERRIDE for the item's edition folders (None -> use each
edition's detected `movie_edition`). `is_new` / `changed_since_reviewed` are
the rescan-derived attention flags that pin a row to "Needs you".

ImportSessionPreviewRead.title: ImportSessionPreviewRead
ImportSessionPreviewRead.description:
The commit-preview aggregate across every source: how many distinct
titles + files the ACCEPTED rows would adopt in place, and the per-tier file
breakdown ("HD 12 · 4K 8") for the sticky commit bar.

ImportSessionRead.title: ImportSessionRead
ImportSessionRead.description:
The whole triage payload: the session header (`status`/`updated_at` drive
the "Draft · auto-saved" bar), the Sources rail, the merged items across all
child scans with decisions applied, and the commit preview.

ImportSessionRescanRequest.title: ImportSessionRescanRequest
ImportSessionRescanRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/import/session/{id}/rescan` body. `scan_id` rescans that ONE
source (the Sources rail's per-card rescan); omitted rescans every child
scan of the session.

ImportSessionSourceRead.title: ImportSessionSourceRead
ImportSessionSourceRead.description:
One child scan of the session -- the Sources rail card. `path` is the
root folder's on-disk path (empty if the root was deleted); `items`/`files`
are the proposed-item and non-rejected-file counts of this scan's result.

ImportSessionStatus.title: ImportSessionStatus
ImportSessionStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a resumable Library-Import triage session (#115).

A ``DRAFT`` session is the auto-saved triage workspace (parent of one child
``ImportScan`` per root). ``COMMITTING`` is the transient state while the
backgrounded commit runner adopts the accepted rows (the row carries a live
progress bar); ``COMMITTED`` when that finishes (files adopted,
``commit_result`` stored); ``FAILED`` if the commit runner errored (or a
restart-orphaned ``COMMITTING`` could not be rebuilt); ``DISCARDED`` when the
user drops the draft (soft; files on disk are untouched -- commit is the only
writer). Lowercase wire values, ``native_enum=False`` (mirrors
``ImportScanStatus``).

ImportSessionSummaryRead.title: ImportSessionSummaryRead
ImportSessionSummaryRead.description:
A light row for `GET /api/v1/import/sessions` (resume the active draft or
list recent imports). `sources` is the child scan count; the tallies mirror
the triage workspace so the launcher's Resume hero shows the same
Matched / Needs-you / Ready / Files counts you'd see inside — `needs_you` and
`ready` partition every item exactly as the modal does (via the same
confidence + rescan-flag rule), `matched` counts items with an (effective)
TMDB id, `titles` the distinct matched titles, and `files` the files to
adopt.

IndexerFlag.title: IndexerFlag
IndexerFlag.description:
arr indexer-flag vocabulary carried on a release (freeleech tiers,
internal, scene, nuked). Persisted on ``MediaFile.indexer_flags`` as the
list of member VALUES.

IndexerResyncResult.title: IndexerResyncResult
IndexerResyncResult.description:
Result of `POST /searchindexers/resync` (INDEXER-WIRING-BE): the number
of arr.Indexer rows re-mirrored into `search_indexers`.

IndexerUnavailableItem.title: IndexerUnavailableItem
IndexerUnavailableItem.description:
INDEXER FAILURE BACKOFF: one indexer currently disabled by failures, for
the top-bar attention control (a FOURTH source, merged like the no-grab
runs). Read-time derived from `SearchIndexer.disabled_till > now`, so it
self-heals -- the row drops the instant a success or the deadline clears the
indexer. `disabled_till` lets the UI render "retries in Xm"; `reason` is the
last error (tooltip). Deep-links Settings > Indexers via `indexer_id`.

IndexerUnavailableSummary.title: IndexerUnavailableSummary
IndexerUnavailableSummary.description:
INDEXER FAILURE BACKOFF: `GET /api/v1/system/indexers/unavailable` -- the
indexers disabled by failures behind the header attention control. Empty
`items` (with `count` 0) is the zero-state (all indexers healthy).

ItemEditionAliasCreate.title: ItemEditionAliasCreate
ItemEditionAliasCreate.description:
#69: `POST /api/v1/library/{item_id}/edition-aliases` body -- add ONE
per-item edition alias.

`term` is the title-specific release term (e.g. "Vrach Frankenshteyn Cut");
trimmed + required non-blank. `edition` is the tracked edition it maps to --
canonicalized server-side and required to match one of THIS item's editions
(a term that maps to no real edition is a 422; the SAME term already mapped to
a DIFFERENT edition is a 409, so a term can never conflate two cuts). `guarded`
(default False) is for a short/ambiguous term (also a plausible title word),
matched only in the trailing edition slot of a movie release.
`extra="forbid"` matches the sibling config request DTOs.

ItemEditionAliasRead.title: ItemEditionAliasRead
ItemEditionAliasRead.description:
#69: one per-item edition alias (see `models.library.ItemEditionAlias`).

`term` is the release-name term to recognise; `edition` is the CANONICAL
tracked-edition string it maps to; `guarded` restricts a short/ambiguous term
to the trailing edition slot of a movie release (the #60 adjacency guard).

Language.title: Language
Language.description:
The canonical language vocabulary (#100).

Mirrors the arr (Sonarr/Radarr) ``Language`` enum EXACTLY -- same ids
(``_LANGUAGE_IDS`` below) and same display names (the member VALUE). Each
member is a ``str`` equal to its display name, so a canonical entry compares
``==`` and ``.lower()``s like the bare name strings the codebase used before
(a persisted/parsed ``[Language.ENGLISH]`` still ``== ["English"]``).

The arr wire identity is the numeric id: use :func:`language_id` /
:func:`language_from_id` for arr-facing translation and :func:`language_from_name`
to resolve a parsed token onto a canonical entry (unresolved -> ``UNKNOWN``).
Persisted on ``MediaFile.languages`` as the list of ids.

LibraryAttentionItem.title: LibraryAttentionItem
LibraryAttentionItem.description:
#113: one edition needing attention, for the global attention control.

Carries enough to deep-link to the edition on its detail page (`item_id` +
`tier`/`movie_edition`) plus the cause-specific `kind`/`message` (built by
`services.attention.edition_attention` -- identical copy to the detail
banner + the Tasks line) and its `root_path` (the affected root).

LibraryAttentionSummary.title: LibraryAttentionSummary
LibraryAttentionSummary.description:
#113: `GET /api/v1/library/attention` -- the data behind the header
attention control. `editions` = how many editions need attention; `titles` =
how many distinct items; `items` = one row per affected edition. Empty
`items` (with `editions`/`titles` 0) is the zero-state -> the control renders
nothing.

LibraryItemEditRequest.title: LibraryItemEditRequest
LibraryItemEditRequest.description:
CA-6 + TRACK-B (#33): body for `PATCH /api/v1/library/{item_id}` --
correct a title's display fields + ID mapping AND edit its item-level
MANAGEMENT (monitored + tags). Every field is optional with *partial*
semantics: only supplied keys are written (`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`
in the route), an omitted field is left untouched, and an explicit `null`
clears a nullable ID mapping (e.g. drop a wrong `imdb_id`). `title` is the
item's only NOT-NULL field, so `title=None`/`""` is rejected (422) by the
route. `extra="forbid"` (unknown field -> 422) matches the sibling
config-mutation request DTOs. Per-EDITION management (profile/root/monitor/
minimum availability) lives on the edition endpoint (`update_edition`).

LibraryRefreshAllResponse.title: LibraryRefreshAllResponse
LibraryRefreshAllResponse.description:
`POST /api/v1/library/refresh-all` -- counts for the library-wide
metadata re-sync (#8: backfills missing tvdb/imdb ids on items added
before the id-translation work).

LogRecordRead.title: LogRecordRead
LogRecordRead.description:
LOG-B1: one captured log record (``GET /api/v1/system/logs``).

Mirrors ``fusionha.services.log_buffer.LogEntry``: the epoch ``ts`` the UI
formats client-side, the level name (DEBUG/INFO/WARNING/ERROR), the emitting
``logger`` name, the rendered ``message``, and the formatted ``traceback``
(present only on records logged with ``exc_info``/``logger.exception``).

LooseFileRead.title: LooseFileRead
LooseFileRead.description:
ITEMACTIONS-BE: one unmatched on-disk video under the item's root(s),
surfaced by `POST /api/v1/library/{id}/manage-files` for the "Manage files"
UI to map onto an edition (+ episode for a series).

ManageFilesRequest.title: ManageFilesRequest
ManageFilesRequest.description:
ITEMACTIONS-BE: body for `POST /api/v1/library/{id}/manage-files`.

With every field omitted it just LISTS the loose files under the item's
root(s). Supplying `path` + `edition_id` MAPS that loose file onto the
edition in place (no move) -- a series map additionally requires
`episode_id`. `extra="forbid"` (unknown field -> 422) matches the sibling
request DTOs.

ManageFilesResponse.title: ManageFilesResponse
ManageFilesResponse.description:
ITEMACTIONS-BE: result of a manage-files call -- the file just mapped (if
any) plus the loose files still awaiting a mapping.

ManagedFileRow.title: ManagedFileRow
ManagedFileRow.description:
One row of the Manage-Episodes bulk editor (arr-parity manual manage).

A flat, self-contained view of one registered on-disk file: its edition +
tier, the season/episode(s) it maps to (empty for a movie file), and every
attribute the bulk editor can display or override. `languages` are canonical
display names; `indexer_flags` the stored `IndexerFlag` values.

ManagedFilesResponse.title: ManagedFilesResponse
ManagedFilesResponse.description:
The Manage-Episodes read model: every registered file of the item as a
flat row. Returned by `GET /api/v1/library/{id}/files` and by the bulk-edit
POST (refreshed rows after the override).

ManualImportCommitRowResult.title: ManualImportCommitRowResult
ManualImportCommitRowResult.description: The per-row outcome of a commit (success carries the created ids).

ManualImportMatchRead.title: ManualImportMatchRead
ManualImportMatchRead.description: The existing library item this file matched (or a null no-match).

ManualImportOverrideRequest.title: ManualImportOverrideRequest
ManualImportOverrideRequest.description:
`POST /manualimport/scan/{id}/override` -- partial per-row override.

Partial semantics: only fields present in the body are applied
(`model_fields_set`); an explicit `null` clears (e.g. `movie_edition`).

ManualImportParsedRead.title: ManualImportParsedRead
ManualImportParsedRead.description: What the parser read off one filename (surfaced for the review UI).

ManualImportScanRead.title: ManualImportScanRead
ManualImportScanRead.description: `GET /manualimport/scan/{id}` -- the persisted scan + its rows + counts.

ManualImportScanRequest.title: ManualImportScanRequest
ManualImportScanRequest.description: `POST /manualimport/scan` body: the source folder to scan.

ManualImportTargetRead.title: ManualImportTargetRead
ManualImportTargetRead.description: The resolved import target: (tier, cut) edition + episode.

MediaFileBlocklistTargetRead.title: MediaFileBlocklistTargetRead
MediaFileBlocklistTargetRead.description:
The release `DELETE /library/files/{id}?blocklist=true` would blocklist
-- resolved from the file's owning grab `Download` (matched by
`imported_media_file_id`). Served by `GET
/library/files/{id}/blocklist-target` (a separate route rather than a field
on `MediaFileRead`, so the heavy item-detail read never pays an extra
per-file query -- this is only fetched when the delete confirm opens).
`null` when the file has no owning grab (hand-placed / library-imported),
which is the signal the confirm's "Also blocklist this release" opt-in
disables against.

MediaFileUpdate.title: MediaFileUpdate
MediaFileUpdate.description:
ITEMACTIONS-BE / #120: body for `PATCH /api/v1/library/files/{file_id}` --
the "Edit Movie File" editor (Radarr parity), also used for the Files-tab
"edit quality" correction. Every field is OPTIONAL and only applied when the
key is present (partial `PATCH` semantics via `model_fields_set`), mirroring
the Manage-Episodes bulk editor (:class:`BulkFileEditRequest`) on a single
file:

* `quality` overrides the parsed quality (`null` is ignored -- quality is
  never cleared).
* `release_group` is free text applied VERBATIM; an empty string / `null`
  CLEARS it.
* `languages` / `indexer_flags` REPLACE the file's set (an empty list
  clears); validated against the canonical `Language` / `IndexerFlag` enums.
* `proper` / `real` set the arr revision (#95/#109): `proper` bumps the
  file's `proper_version` (True -> 1, False -> 0), `real` flags a REAL
  re-release. Both feed the Proper/Repack + Real custom-format scoring; a
  `null` is a no-op.

After any change the file's CF score is re-derived. `extra="forbid"`
(unknown field -> 422) matches the sibling config-mutation request DTOs.

MediaIssueCreate.title: MediaIssueCreate
MediaIssueCreate.description:
`POST /api/v1/issues` — report a problem with an on-server title.

`scope` narrows the report: `item` (whole title, the default), `season`
(requires `season`), or `episode` (requires `season` + `episode`). The
validator 422s a season/episode scope missing its coordinates. `description`
is the reporter's free text. The reporter is ALWAYS the calling principal's
user (the route never trusts a client-supplied reporter id).

MediaIssueRead.title: MediaIssueRead
MediaIssueRead.description:
A reported issue. `resolved` is a DERIVED convenience
(`status == resolved`) so a client need not compare the enum.

MediaIssueResolve.title: MediaIssueResolve
MediaIssueResolve.description: `POST /api/v1/issues/{id}/resolve` — close an issue with an optional note.

MediaIssueScope.title: MediaIssueScope
MediaIssueScope.description:
How narrowly a :class:`~fusionha.models.issues.MediaIssue` is scoped.

``ITEM`` is the whole title (the default); ``SEASON`` carries a ``season``;
``EPISODE`` carries ``season`` + ``episode``. Only meaningful for a series --
a movie issue is always ``ITEM``.

MediaIssueStatus.title: MediaIssueStatus
MediaIssueStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a :class:`~fusionha.models.issues.MediaIssue`.

``OPEN`` on report; ``RESOLVED`` once an ``issues.manage`` holder (or an
admin) closes it (stamping ``resolved_by`` / ``resolved_at`` + an optional
``comment``).

MediaIssueType.title: MediaIssueType
MediaIssueType.description:
What KIND of problem a :class:`~fusionha.models.issues.MediaIssue` reports
on an on-server title (P3a Issue reporting -- the requestor-experience flow).

Lowercase wire values (like :class:`RequestStatus`); persisted as the member
NAME via ``native_enum=False`` (VARCHAR + CHECK), matching every other enum
column in the schema.

MediaRequestCreate.title: MediaRequestCreate
MediaRequestCreate.description:
`POST /api/v1/requests` — submit a request for a title at one-or-more editions.

P2a multi-edition: `editions` is the authoritative tier set; `tier` is a
back-compat shorthand — when `editions` is omitted it becomes `[tier]`, and
the primary `tier` is set from `editions[0]` when only `editions` is given.
For a series, `seasons` / `episodes` scope the ask (empty ⇒ whole series).

`user_id` lets an identity-less allow-all caller (auth-off / trusted app key)
name the owner (there is no session identity); a logged-in caller omits it
(or passes their own id). `note` is optional free text.

MediaRequestRead.title: MediaRequestRead
MediaRequestRead.description:
A request row. `status` may read the DERIVED `fulfilled` (never stored):
an approved request whose edition owns a file surfaces as `fulfilled`.

`quota_exceeded` is a response-only flag set on an approve (or auto-approve)
that pushed the requester past their weekly quota — SURFACED, never enforced;
False on every plain read/list.

MergeGrantPreview.title: MergeGrantPreview
MergeGrantPreview.description: One resulting AccessGrant after the union (`instance_id=None` = wildcard).

MergePreviewRead.title: MergePreviewRead
MergePreviewRead.description:
The EFFECTIVE resulting state of a merge (the dry-run preview, or what an
execute did) -- the resulting role/permission/capability/grant set, not just
row re-point counts (INV4).

MergeRequest.title: MergeRequest
MergeRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/{survivor}/merge` -- fold `loser` into the survivor.

`role_resolution` defaults to keeping the survivor's role (no escalation);
`adopt_loser` is amplification-checked. `dry_run` (default True) returns the
effective-resulting preview WITHOUT mutating -- an explicit `dry_run=false`
executes (the operator is expected to have taken a backup first).

MetadataSwitchCommitRequest.title: MetadataSwitchCommitRequest
MetadataSwitchCommitRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /library/{id}/metadata-switch/commit``. ``rename_files``
False is "switch only, keep filenames" (still a completed commit -- the
provider IS set). ``exclude_file_ids`` drops user-unchecked (e.g.
``title-only-warn``) files from the rename. ``expected_hash`` is the preview's
``diff_hash`` echoed verbatim; a mismatch (the series/target changed) is a 409,
never a silent re-apply of a different diff.

MetadataSwitchDispatchRead.title: MetadataSwitchDispatchRead
MetadataSwitchDispatchRead.description:
202 body of ``POST /library/{id}/metadata-switch/commit``: the opened
``CommandRun`` id, polled via ``GET /system/runs/{run_id}`` for its
``metadata_switch_summary`` once terminal.

MetadataSwitchFileMatch.title: MetadataSwitchFileMatch
MetadataSwitchFileMatch.description:
One series file's raw-name -> target-episode matching (the Detailed raw-file
view). ``confidence`` is ``sxxexx`` (numeric-confident) / ``title`` /
``title-only-warn`` (flagged, default included) / ``unmatched`` (never
auto-renamed). ``included`` defaults True; a caller sends the excluded ids on
commit.

MetadataSwitchMatchRead.title: MetadataSwitchMatchRead
MetadataSwitchMatchRead.description:
The confirmed target-provider series a switch would pull from (the modal's
Match step).

MetadataSwitchPreviewRead.title: MetadataSwitchPreviewRead
MetadataSwitchPreviewRead.description:
``POST /library/{id}/metadata-switch/preview`` -- a read-only DIFF (no
writes): the confirmed/needs-search target match, the season/episode reconcile
(reusing the numbering diff shapes), the per-file raw matching, and a
``diff_hash`` the client echoes back on commit so a stale preview can never be
blind-applied.

MetadataSwitchPreviewRequest.title: MetadataSwitchPreviewRequest
MetadataSwitchPreviewRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /library/{id}/metadata-switch/preview``. ``target_provider``
is the source to switch TO (``tmdb``, ``tvdb``, or ``hybrid``). ``target_id`` is
OPTIONAL (and ignored for ``hybrid``):
omit it to auto-resolve the target series from the item's ids/title (the modal
confirms the match), or pass a user-chosen id to override a wrong/low-confidence
auto-match.

MetadataSwitchResultRead.title: MetadataSwitchResultRead
MetadataSwitchResultRead.description:
The materialised outcome of a completed switch, retained on the run-capture
summary channel and surfaced as ``CommandRunDetailRead.metadata_switch_summary``
once terminal.

MetadataSwitchUndoRead.title: MetadataSwitchUndoRead
MetadataSwitchUndoRead.description:
200 body of ``POST /library/{id}/metadata-switch/undo``: the reverted
provider + counts of what was rolled back.

MinimumAvailability.title: MinimumAvailability
MinimumAvailability.description:
Radarr per-movie ``minimumAvailability`` (when a movie becomes grabbable).

Wire values match Radarr verbatim; persisted onto ``QualityEdition``'s
existing ``minimum_availability`` string column and surfaced by each virtual
instance's MovieResource (arrapi/mappers.py, which defaults NULL -> released).

MonitorToggleRequest.title: MonitorToggleRequest
MonitorToggleRequest.description:
CA-2: body for the season/episode monitoring toggle endpoints -- the
single `monitored` flag flipped on one Season/Episode row. `extra="forbid"`
(an unknown field -> 422) matches the other config-mutation request DTOs.

MoveCredentialRequest.title: MoveCredentialRequest
MoveCredentialRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/{id}/credentials/{cid}/move` -- re-point one credential
onto `target_user_id`. system.admin + amplification against the target (INV3).

MovieFileBulkDeletePayload.title: MovieFileBulkDeletePayload
MovieFileBulkDeletePayload.description:
Radarr v3 `DELETE /moviefile/bulk` body — the movie-file (MediaFile) ids
to delete. Used by decypharr's blocking to drop a rejected download's file.

MovieFileResource.title: MovieFileResource
MovieFileResource.description:
Radarr v3 `movieFile` (embedded in MovieResource and served at
`GET /moviefile`). Minimal-but-faithful subset: the fields fusionha tracks
per `MediaFile`, with `quality` mapped through the flavor-keyed
`qualityname_to_ref` table (#47a).

NotificationAgentCreate.title: NotificationAgentCreate
NotificationAgentCreate.description:
Connect (T-CONNECT): a fusionha-native Discord/Telegram/generic-webhook
notification agent. Mirrors `SearchIndexerCreate`'s shape -- `url`/`token`
are secret-preserving fields.

NotificationKind.title: NotificationKind
NotificationKind.description:
Connect (fusionha-native notification agents, T-CONNECT) provider kind.

Distinct from the arr-emulation `/api/v3/notification` surface
(`fusionha.models.arr.ArrNotification`) -- that mirrors what Overseerr/
decypharr register on a virtual instance; this is fusionha's OWN
Discord/Telegram/generic-webhook agents, configured once and firing on
fusionha's own library events (grab/import/upgrade/manual-required/
failed) regardless of which arr-emulation clients are attached.

NotificationPreferenceItem.title: NotificationPreferenceItem
NotificationPreferenceItem.description: One (event, enabled) row of the push opt-in matrix.

NotificationPreferencesRead.title: NotificationPreferencesRead
NotificationPreferencesRead.description: A principal's full push opt-in matrix (every event; stored-or-default).

NotificationPreferencesUpdate.title: NotificationPreferencesUpdate
NotificationPreferencesUpdate.description:
Set some/all of a principal's push opt-in rows.

``principal_id`` targets another user (admin-equivalent only). Only listed
events are written; omitted events keep their stored row / built-in default.

NotificationResource.title: NotificationResource
NotificationResource.description:
arr v3 notification connection (#58) -- the shape decypharr POSTs when
registering its Webhook and reads back from GET /notification. Persisted
per virtual instance (``ArrNotification``); flags fusionha doesn't act on
are echoed with arr defaults, and `extra="ignore"` (ArrResource) tolerates
the many onX flags real arr clients send that aren't modelled here.

NumberingApplyDispatchRead.title: NumberingApplyDispatchRead
NumberingApplyDispatchRead.description:
202 body of ``POST /library/{id}/numbering/apply``: the freshly-opened
``CommandRun`` id, polled via ``GET /system/runs/{run_id}`` (its
``numbering_summary`` once terminal) -- mirrors ``RefreshDispatchRead``.

NumberingApplyRequest.title: NumberingApplyRequest
NumberingApplyRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /library/{id}/numbering/apply``. ``expected_hash`` is the
``diff_hash`` echoed verbatim from the preview this confirm dialog rendered;
a mismatch (the series/source changed since the preview) is a 409, never a
silent re-apply of a different diff.

``source`` is OPTIONAL (#180 P4): omit it to let the apply route default from
the series' resolved metadata provider (tvdb/hybrid -> tvdb, else tvmaze) --
the SAME resolution the preview uses, so the two never disagree on which
source the ``expected_hash`` was built against. A confirm dialog should echo
the RESOLVED ``source`` the preview returned so the pin is explicit.

NumberingApplyResultRead.title: NumberingApplyResultRead
NumberingApplyResultRead.description:
The materialised outcome of a completed numbering apply (mirrors
``services.episode_numbering_apply.NumberingApplyResult``), retained on the
run-capture summary channel and surfaced as
``CommandRunDetailRead.numbering_summary`` once the run goes terminal.

NumberingDiffRowRead.title: NumberingDiffRowRead
NumberingDiffRowRead.description:
One line of the TMDB(current)-vs-alternate numbering diff (mirrors
``services.episode_numbering.NumberingRow``). ``kind`` is one of
``unchanged``/``renumbered``/``retitled``/``added``/``removed``; exactly one
of the number pair is ``None`` for an add/remove.

NumberingPreviewRead.title: NumberingPreviewRead
NumberingPreviewRead.description:
``GET /library/{id}/numbering/preview`` -- a read-only projection of what
:func:`services.episode_numbering_apply.apply_numbering` WOULD change, plus a
``diff_hash`` the client must echo back on
``POST /library/{id}/numbering/apply`` so a stale preview can never be
blind-applied (the apply route recomputes the diff server-side and 409s on a
mismatch).

NumberingResetResult.title: NumberingResetResult
NumberingResetResult.description:
200 body of ``POST /library/{id}/numbering/reset``: the item's numbering
override state right after the flag is cleared (always
``episode_numbering_source=None`` -- the next metadata refresh re-adopts
TMDB).

OfferableEditionsRead.title: OfferableEditionsRead
OfferableEditionsRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/requests/offerable` — the editions the CURRENT principal may
request for a title (P2a access-scoped offering).

`editions` = policy-allowed ∩ per-instance-visible ∩ not-already-owned, so the
request modal renders ONLY these. `mode` is the requester's
`request_quality_mode`; in `auto` mode there is no picker and `auto_editions`
is the admin-fixed set that will be requested (equal to `editions`), while in
`choose` mode `auto_editions` is empty.

ParkedItemPoster.title: ParkedItemPoster
ParkedItemPoster.description:
Artwork for a parked dock chip -- a poster URL, a gradient fallback, or
both (mirrors the frontend `ParkedPoster`).

ParkedItemRead.title: ParkedItemRead
ParkedItemRead.description:
One parked dock descriptor for a user's dock (#174 Phase E).

The JSON shape mirrors the frontend `ParkedItem` (camelCase `scrollTop` /
`expiresAt`) so the dock hydrates the array straight from the API. `live` is
a device-local hint; a hydrated descriptor is resumed live only when THIS
tab still holds its keep-alive subtree, else it reopens via the reconstruct
path. No sensitive values -- descriptors are UI state, nothing to redact.

ParkedItemWrite.title: ParkedItemWrite
ParkedItemWrite.description:
Create/replace one parked descriptor. `id` is the stable dock id (all
mutators keyed by it); `mediaItemId` is the optional media-item ref so
deleting a title cascades its dock chips (also best-effort parsed from a
`search:<id>:` id server-side when omitted).

ParkedItemsReplace.title: ParkedItemsReplace
ParkedItemsReplace.description:
The coalesced full-list persist: replace the caller's ENTIRE dock with
`items` (list order = dock order).

PlexConnectResult.title: PlexConnectResult
PlexConnectResult.description:
Plex SSO admin auto-config: result of the `POST /settings/plex/connect/
{id}/check` poll. `status` is `pending` (still awaiting the browser authorise)
or `connected` (the owner token was captured and the owned server resolved +
persisted). Never echoes the captured token -- only the resolved public facts
(spec §8/§10.4).

PlexImportResult.title: PlexImportResult
PlexImportResult.description:
Plex SSO: result of `POST /api/v1/settings/plex-import` -- the number of
shared users provisioned as Requestors on this run (spec §8).

PlexPinRead.title: PlexPinRead
PlexPinRead.description:
Plex SSO: result of `POST /api/v1/auth/plex/pin`. The browser is sent to
`authUrl` to authorise `code`; the SPA then polls `.../pin/{id}/check`.

PlexPruneResult.title: PlexPruneResult
PlexPruneResult.description:
Plex SSO: result of `POST /api/v1/settings/plex-prune` -- the
auto-provisioned Requestor accounts DELETED this run because they can no
longer sign in (revoked share / excluded home user). ``removed`` is the
count; ``usernames`` names each pruned account. Empty (0/[]) when the live
Plex membership fetch fails -- pruning never deletes on an incomplete fetch.

PlexTestResult.title: PlexTestResult
PlexTestResult.description:
Plex SSO: result of `POST /api/v1/settings/test-plex`. Validates the owner
token by resolving the owner identity + owned server + membership set. Never
echoes the token -- only the resolved public facts (spec §8/§10.4).

PresetAdoptRequest.title: PresetAdoptRequest
PresetAdoptRequest.description:
`POST /presets/{id}/adopt`: CLAIM an existing quality profile for this
preset (set only the ownership link), so a later deploy can rebuild it in
place. The 0081 migration does no backfill, so a pre-link profile must be
adopted before it can be replaced.

PresetCaptureRequest.title: PresetCaptureRequest
PresetCaptureRequest.description:
`POST /presets/capture`: read `profile_name` from the connection's arr
and store its manifest. `media_kind` defaults from the connection flavor
(sonarr->series, radarr->movie); pass `anime` explicitly for a
Sonarr-anime instance. `name` is the stored preset name (e.g. capture a
Sonarr `HD-1080p` as `HD-1080p-Series`); it defaults to the arr profile
name.

PresetDeployRequest.title: PresetDeployRequest
PresetDeployRequest.description:
`POST /presets/{id}/deploy`. `conflict` is the global policy for CFs
that already exist in fusionha (skip keeps the existing definition,
overwrite reimports from the guide); `per_format` overrides it per
manifest key (the review dialog's Decide-each mode).

PresetDeployResult.title: PresetDeployResult
PresetDeployResult.description:
Deploy outcome: the created profile + per-CF import counts. `unresolved`
lists manifest entries neither imported, found in the guide bundle, nor
spec-captured (their scores were dropped).

PresetFormatSpec.title: PresetFormatSpec
PresetFormatSpec.description:
One snapshotted custom-format specification in a manifest's
`format_specs` entry (the cf_import spec mapping, serialised).

PresetManifest.title: PresetManifest
PresetManifest.description:
The portable captured-profile document. `allowed_qualities`/`cutoff`
are fusionha QualityName values; `format_scores` keys are TRaSH ids when
resolvable against the guide bundle, CF names otherwise. `format_specs`
snapshots the full spec definitions of name-keyed entries (arr CFs the
guide doesn't know) so deploy can create them outright; absent on
manifests captured before #59.

`quality_groups` / `cutoff_group` / `cutoff_group_index` carry the source
arr's quality GROUPING (and a group-valued arr cutoff: `cutoff_group` is its
readable name, `cutoff_group_index` its position in `quality_groups` -- the
unambiguous identity, since arr group names may collide). All are optional
and nothing is inferred: a manifest captured before they existed deploys as
a flat ladder exactly as it does today, and a name-only `cutoff_group` still
resolves.

EVERY field is optional-with-a-default and read tolerantly, because this is
the READ side of a document `deploy_preset` accepts hostile -- see the rule
above the helpers. A required/strict field was a 500 out of `GET /presets`
for a row that deploys fine: a null or absent `name`, `media_kind: []`,
`allowed_qualities: 5`, `cutoff: []`, `upgrade: 5`, `format_scores: []`, a
score of `"x"`, junk `format_specs`. The served VALUE is the one the deploy
would use, never an invented one.

PresetQualityGroup.title: PresetQualityGroup
PresetQualityGroup.description:
One captured arr quality GROUP: its members rank EQUAL in the deployed
profile, so the custom-format score decides between them (a rank difference
short-circuits the upgrade check before the score is read). `qualities` are
fusionha QualityName values, contiguous within the manifest's
`allowed_qualities`. `allowed` is carried for shape parity with the TRaSH
bundle and the profile editor's grouped `items[]` entry; deploy always
builds an allowed group.

`name` is NOT an identity -- arr does not enforce unique group names inside
a profile, so two entries with the same name are two distinct groups. A
group's identity is its POSITION in `quality_groups` (the manifest carries
no arr ids), which is what `cutoff_group_index` refers to.

PresetRead.title: PresetRead
PresetRead.description:
A stored preset. `deploy_name` is the kind-suffixed default profile
name a deploy would use (`<name>-<Kind>[-4K]`, the #55 dash naming
standard), always overridable.

PresetRenameRequest.title: PresetRenameRequest
PresetRenameRequest.description:
`PATCH /presets/{id}`: rename a stored preset. The manifest's `name`
(and thus the default deploy name) follows. 409 when the `(name,
media_kind)` pair is already taken.

PresetUnresolvedScore.title: PresetUnresolvedScore
PresetUnresolvedScore.description:
One manifest score deploy could not attach: the manifest key (trash_id
or CF name) plus the score that was dropped.

PresetUpgradeSettings.title: PresetUpgradeSettings
PresetUpgradeSettings.description:
The manifest's upgrade block (arr upgrade rules, fusionha field names).

Every field is read the way `deploy_preset` reads it: an unusable block or
value degrades to the SAME default the deployed profile would carry, so the
read never contradicts the deploy (`upgrade: 5` handed the scalar itself to
`.get` here and 422ed the whole list; it deploys as these defaults).

PreviewEpisode.title: PreviewEpisode
PreviewEpisode.description:
One episode of a season, from TMDB (`EpisodeMeta`), read-only. Fetched
lazily (`GET /preview/{kind}/{tmdb_id}/season/{n}`) when the request modal
expands a season, so the picker can show real episode titles pre-add.

PreviewSeason.title: PreviewSeason
PreviewSeason.description:
One season summary from TMDB (`SeasonMeta`): season number + episode
count, read-only. The preview view lists these without fetching each
season's episode tree (that only exists once the item is added).

PushDeviceTestResult.title: PushDeviceTestResult
PushDeviceTestResult.description: The outcome of a test send to ONE device.

PushSubscriptionCreate.title: PushSubscriptionCreate
PushSubscriptionCreate.description:
Register (or re-register) one device push subscription.

Bound to the caller's principal. ``principal_id`` is honoured ONLY for an
admin-equivalent caller acting on another user's behalf (or a headless
allow-all caller with no session identity); a regular user's value must be
its own id (else 403).

PushSubscriptionRead.title: PushSubscriptionRead
PushSubscriptionRead.description: One device subscription -- the device encryption keys are NOT echoed.

PushTestResult.title: PushTestResult
PushTestResult.description: The aggregate test-send outcome across the caller's devices.

QualityModel.title: QualityModel
QualityModel.description:
arr's nested quality payload as carried by movieFile/episodeFile/history
resources: `{quality: {id, name, source, resolution, modifier}, revision}`
(#47a / quality-model-expansion §6.3).

QualityProfileGroupResource.title: QualityProfileGroupResource
QualityProfileGroupResource.description:
A GROUP entry in a v3 profile's `items` ladder: a named bundle of
qualities that rank as EQUAL, with its members NESTED in its own `items`.

arr parity: a group entry carries `id` + `name` and NO `quality` key, and
its `id` lives in the >= 1000 range so it can never collide with a
quality id (which are 0..~30 per app) -- a group-valued profile `cutoff`
is that id.

QualityProfileItemResource.title: QualityProfileItemResource
QualityProfileItemResource.description:
A LEAF entry in a v3 profile's `items` ladder: one quality.

arr emits `"items": []` on a leaf (the nesting slot a group would fill) and
NO `id`/`name` -- that absence is exactly how a client tells a quality entry
from a group entry, so the two shapes stay separate models.

QualityRevision.title: QualityRevision
QualityRevision.description:
arr's `revision` block inside a file/history quality model. fusionha
folds REMUX/proper-ness into `QualityName` and never tracks re-releases, so
the honest static defaults (v1, not-real, not-a-repack) are emitted.

QueueProcessResult.title: QueueProcessResult
QueueProcessResult.description:
Result of `POST /api/v1/queue/process` -- ONE on-demand import-poll pass
forced from the Activity → Queue tab's "Process queue now" button, so the
user need not wait for the ~60s scheduled cadence.

The same counts the scheduled import-poll tick logs
(`runtime._run_import_poll_counts`): how many non-terminal downloads were
`in_flight` at the start, how many `imported` this pass, how many otherwise
`resolved` (failed/reconciled/adopted), and how many are `left` still
non-terminal. `skipped` is `True` (with zeroed counts) when
`real_integrations` is off -- a queue-scoped pass has nothing to do with
integrations disabled -- or when a benign concurrent-removal race rolled the
pass back; the endpoint still returns HTTP 200 in that case, never a 5xx.

RefreshDispatchRead.title: RefreshDispatchRead
RefreshDispatchRead.description:
#136: the 202 body of ``POST /library/{id}/refresh``. The heavy Refresh &
Scan now runs in a background task; the route returns immediately with the id
of the opened ``CommandRun`` so the frontend can poll ``/system/runs/{run_id}``
for live progress and, on completion, the ``rescan_summary``.

RegrabRequest.title: RegrabRequest
RegrabRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/v1/history/{history_id}/regrab`. ``override`` mirrors the
interactive grab route's grab-anyway: when the exact release is blocklisted,
``override=True`` clears the matching block first, then re-grabs.

RegrabResultRead.title: RegrabResultRead
RegrabResultRead.description:
Outcome of a re-grab attempt (`services.regrab.RegrabResult`). Returned
with a 200 for BOTH a successful re-grab and a clean no-match (the latter is
not an error -- it just grabbed nothing). ``from_original_indexer`` is True
when the exact release was re-found on the indexer it was originally grabbed
from, False when a DIFFERENT indexer supplied it, and None when nothing was
grabbed. ``reason`` carries the user-facing no-grab explanation (None on a
successful grab).

ReleaseScopeStatusRead.title: ReleaseScopeStatusRead
ReleaseScopeStatusRead.description:
SEARCH-TRANSPARENCY B2: why a scope's AUTO-search is (or isn't) paused.

USER REPORT ("auto grabs nothing but interactive has many", #148 family):
three independent silencers pause auto-search for a scope with no surfaced
reason -- the per-(edition, season) ``BacklogBackoffService`` backoff, the
per-(edition, episode) ``FailureCadenceService`` failed-grab cooldown, and a
run of empty passes. Interactive Search bypasses all three, so the modal
listed many releases while auto looked idle and unexplained. This read-only
shape lets the modal render "auto paused until HH:MM (N empty searches)" /
"cooling down after N failed downloads" instead of a silent gap.

ReleaseTermKind.title: ReleaseTermKind
ReleaseTermKind.description:
#70: a global release-title term filter (arr "Release Profiles"). A
``REQUIRED`` term the release title MUST match (≥1 of the required set); a
``REJECTED`` term it must NOT match. Plain case-insensitive substring, or a
regex when the term is wrapped in ``/.../``.

ReleaseTermTestRequest.title: ReleaseTermTestRequest
ReleaseTermTestRequest.description: Try a candidate release title against the current enabled term filters.

ReleaseTermTestResult.title: ReleaseTermTestResult
ReleaseTermTestResult.description:
Whether the title would be grabbed, and (if not) the rejection reason --
computed by the SAME matcher the grab gate uses (one source of truth).

ReleaseType.title: ReleaseType
ReleaseType.description:
arr (Sonarr) ReleaseType -- how many episodes a release carries.

Values match arr's ``singleEpisode``/``multiEpisode``/``seasonPack`` token
vocabulary (the same tokens ``services.trash._RELEASE_TYPE_BY_ID`` resolves
arr enum ids onto). Persisted on ``MediaFile.release_type`` (default
``UNKNOWN`` -- movies and pre-existing rows).

ReleaseWindowRead.title: ReleaseWindowRead
ReleaseWindowRead.description:
HOVER-STAGE: one computed release window for a MOVIE's detail release
strip (`services.release_stage.movie_release_windows`).

`kind` is `cinema`/`digital`/`physical`; `date` the window's date; `estimated`
True when it was projected from the cinema anchor (+45d digital, +90d
physical) because TMDB carries no typed date for it (confirmed dates always
win). Lets the frontend render estimated Digital/Physical pills HONESTLY from
a single backend source rather than inventing them.

RelinkAuditRead.title: RelinkAuditRead
RelinkAuditRead.description:
``GET /library/{id}/relink-audit`` -- a read-only report comparing every
series file's true content identity (symlink target) to its current episode
link. ``clean`` is True when nothing needs repair.

RelinkMismatchRead.title: RelinkMismatchRead
RelinkMismatchRead.description:
One file whose true content identity (from its symlink target) differs
from the episode(s) it is currently linked to.

RelinkRepairResultRead.title: RelinkRepairResultRead
RelinkRepairResultRead.description:
200 body of ``POST /library/{id}/relink-repair``: what the apply moved,
what it could not (``unparseable``), the source-collisions it REFUSED to
merge (``conflicts``), and how many on-disk symlinks it renamed.

RelinkSourceCollisionRead.title: RelinkSourceCollisionRead
RelinkSourceCollisionRead.description:
Two or more distinct files whose true identity is the SAME episode -- the
repair refuses to merge them.

RenameApplyResponse.title: RenameApplyResponse
RenameApplyResponse.description:
How many files a rename moved -- and every file it refused to move.

``skipped`` is ADDITIVE (default ``[]``): before it, an operator who clicked
"Rename Files" and got ``applied: 0`` was told nothing at all, while the
only explanation sat in a ``logger.warning`` inside the container.

RenamePreviewRead.title: RenamePreviewRead
RenamePreviewRead.description:
One file in a rename batch: a move, or a refusal.

Serialized with the arr-familiar ``from``/``to`` keys (Python keywords, so
the fields are named ``from_path``/``to_path`` with serialization aliases).

``blocked``/``reason``/``blocked_by_*`` are ADDITIVE and default to the
"this is an ordinary move" values, so the GET's default array is unchanged
for every existing client. A blocked row appears in the GET only under
``include_blocked=true``; it appears unconditionally in
``RenameApplyResponse.skipped``, because that is the moment the operator is
waiting for an answer and the runtime refusals (a missing source, an
untracked squatter on the destination) exist nowhere else.

RenameSkipReason.title: RenameSkipReason
RenameSkipReason.description:
Why a rename REFUSED to move a file.

A rename never overwrites a file, so a file can be dropped from the batch
for four distinct reasons -- each with a DIFFERENT operator remedy, which is
why this is an enum and not a bool. Surfaced on
``RenamePreviewRead.reason`` (GET, with ``include_blocked``) and on
``RenameApplyResponse.skipped`` (POST), so "Rename Files did nothing" is
always explained on the wire rather than only in the container log.

Declared HERE rather than in :mod:`fusionha.enums` because it is produced by
this service and is never persisted to a column (no Alembic migration): it
exists only in a response body, and the DTO layer imports it from its
producer.

ReplaceSearchResult.title: ReplaceSearchResult
ReplaceSearchResult.description: The edition-scoped search dispatched after a successful Replace delete.

RequestReason.title: RequestReason
RequestReason.description:
Why a :class:`~fusionha.models.requests.MediaRequest` was rejected/deferred.

Set only on a decline/defer decision (an optional free-text ``note`` may
accompany it); NULL on pending/approved/fulfilled rows.

RequestRejectRequest.title: RequestRejectRequest
RequestRejectRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/requests/{id}/reject` — decline (or defer) with a REQUIRED
reason. `defer=True` records a temporary `deferred` ("not available yet")
that stays on the requester's list; otherwise `rejected`.

RequestStatus.title: RequestStatus

RescanSummary.title: RescanSummary
RescanSummary.description:
P1 (dead-file UX): the outcome of the manual "Refresh & Scan"
(:class:`fusionha.services.library_import.rescan.RescanOutcome`), surfaced on
the refresh response so the toast reports what actually happened instead of a
generic "done". Every count is CAUSE-NEUTRAL: `flagged` is "files that
couldn't be resolved on the last scan" (NOT diagnosed deletions -- nothing was
removed for them), `removed` is the confirmed-over-the-safety-window prune,
and `standdown` lists edition ids whose root was unreachable (a dark/offline
mount) so the reconcile stood down -- a "library folder unreachable" context,
never a per-file cause claim.

ResolveTvdbIdRead.title: ResolveTvdbIdRead
ResolveTvdbIdRead.description:
#180 Fix B: the body of ``POST /library/{id}/resolve-tvdb-id`` -- the manual
escape hatch that runs the corroborated resolver for one series. ``matched``
True carries the resolved ``tvdb_id`` + ``source`` channel; ``matched`` False
carries a short ``reason`` (nothing corroborated -> the id stays NULL, never a
guess).

ResourceBulkDeleteRequest.title: ResourceBulkDeleteRequest
ResourceBulkDeleteRequest.description:
Bulk-delete a set of config resources (quality profiles / custom formats)
by primary key. Mirrors the single-delete in-use guard per id: a resource
still referenced (a profile a `QualityEdition` targets, a CF a
`QualityProfileFormatScore` scores) is reported in the `BulkResult.errors`
and skipped rather than deleted -- the batch never 500s or aborts.

RevokeSessionsResult.title: RevokeSessionsResult
RevokeSessionsResult.description:
`POST /api/v1/users/{id}/revoke-sessions` -- how many live sessions were
signed out. The account stays enabled and its PATs keep working.

RoleCatalogRead.title: RoleCatalogRead
RoleCatalogRead.description:
The assignable-key vocabulary for the Roles editor: every Axis-A
permission key and every Axis-B capability key the backend recognises, so
the editor offers exactly what a create/update will accept (no hardcoded,
drift-prone client list). Sorted for a stable UI order.

RootDisposition.title: RootDisposition
RootDisposition.description:
What to do with an edition's existing files when its root folder changes
(native edit + arr `moveFiles`). Lowercase wire values match the arr/native
JSON conventions.

RootFolderDefaultSlot.title: RootFolderDefaultSlot
RootFolderDefaultSlot.description:
Phase B: a single `(profile_kind, tier)` Add-defaults slot whose root is
THIS root folder. Surfaces on `RootFolderRead.default_for` so the Root
Folders cards can render a green "Default · <kind> · <tier>" badge without
the client re-joining the add-defaults matrix. Carries only the badge's two
coordinates -- the profile/root FKs live on `AddDefaultSlot` (owned by the
Default Profiles surface). `profile_kind` is the frontend ProfileKind
vocabulary (movie/series/anime); `tier` is the QualityTier.

RunAttentionItem.title: RunAttentionItem
RunAttentionItem.description:
Option B: one manual "stuck no-grab" run for the top-bar attention
control -- a MANUAL search that found releases but grabbed nothing, whose
target is STILL wanted. Mirrors `LibraryAttentionItem` so the frontend
merges it as a third attention source. Carries enough to deep-link the
title's Searches pane (`item_id`) and render the server-built `reason`
verbatim (one source of truth in `services.run_attention`).

RunAttentionSummary.title: RunAttentionSummary
RunAttentionSummary.description:
Option B: `GET /api/v1/system/runs/attention` -- the manual no-grab rows
behind the header attention control. Empty `items` (with `count` 0) is the
zero-state -> the control renders nothing from this source.

RunCandidateAction.title: RunCandidateAction
RunCandidateAction.description:
What the decision engine did with one release in a run.

Mirrors :class:`DecisionAction` (grab/upgrade/reject) but adds ``SKIP`` for
releases the pass considered but neither grabbed nor formally rejected
(e.g. already-grabbed / pre-excluded ghosts). Uppercase wire values so the
decision trail reads like the arr history vocabulary.

RunCandidateRead.title: RunCandidateRead
RunCandidateRead.description:
One release a run considered, with its arr-style action + reason (why).

The decision trail behind a run: `action` (GRAB/UPGRADE/REJECT/SKIP) is the
grouping key the detail view buckets on, `reason` the human "why".

ScopeMismatchDismissed.title: ScopeMismatchDismissed
ScopeMismatchDismissed.description:
`POST /api/v1/library/{id}/scope-mismatch/dismiss` -- the operator's
explicit "I know, leave it as it is" for an anime-scope mismatch row.
Idempotent: `dismissed` is True whether or not a marker was set.

SearchProgressRead.title: SearchProgressRead
SearchProgressRead.description:
Structured live progress + full scope for a RUNNING backlog sweep
(deliverables A/B/D). Present only on a RUNNING missing/cutoff-unmet run;
``None`` on every other run + on any terminal row. ``stuck``/``stalled_seconds``
are computed server-side against the same clock that stamped
``last_progress_at`` (deliverable D) -- no client/server skew. ``stopped`` is
True once Stop was pressed and the current target is finishing.

SearchScopeTargetRead.title: SearchScopeTargetRead
SearchScopeTargetRead.description:
One backlog-sweep target row (deliverable B). ``tier`` is the edition tier
enum value (``"HD-1080p"``/``"UHD-2160p"``) when the target spans a single
monitored edition, else ``None``; ``state`` is the live per-target state as
the loop reaches it (``queued`` -> ``searching`` -> ``grabbed``/``no_release``).

SeriesMonitor.title: SeriesMonitor
SeriesMonitor.description:
Sonarr add-time monitor mode (``addOptions.monitor``).

Wire values match Sonarr v3/v4 verbatim so the native Add flow and the arr
emulation speak the same vocabulary. Applied to a freshly-populated
Season/Episode tree by ``services.library.apply_series_monitor``; the exact
per-mode semantics were verified against a live Sonarr v4 (ADD-1 plan).

SeriesType.title: SeriesType
SeriesType.description:
Sonarr's per-series ``seriesType`` (#53) -- how a series numbers and
names its episodes, driving parsing, search fan-out, release matching, and
file naming:

* ``STANDARD`` -- SxxEyy numbering (``Show S01E05``);
* ``DAILY`` -- date-based numbering (``Show 2020-05-25``): releases are
  matched by ``ParsedRelease.air_date == Episode.air_date`` and named with
  the ``{Air-Date}`` token;
* ``ANIME`` -- absolute numbering (``Show - 005``): absolute-number query
  fan-out + matching and the anime naming format.

Wire values match Sonarr verbatim (``standard``/``daily``/``anime``); the
DB column persists the member NAME (``Enum`` stores names, like every other
enum column here). Stored on ``MediaItem.series_type`` as the source of
truth; the legacy ``is_anime`` flag is kept in sync on writes
(``is_anime == (series_type is ANIME)``) for back-compat readers.

SessionEnrichmentRead.title: SessionEnrichmentRead
SessionEnrichmentRead.description:
The per-session post-import enrichment task (#153) surfaced on a session
read. Scoped to just THIS import job's adopted files (not the whole library):
`control` is the user's pause/resume/cancel state and `state` is derived
(`cancelled` / `paused` / `complete` once nothing is pending / `analyzing`
while the sweep still has files). A DRAFT session has no adopted files -> all
zeros. `issues` is the bounded stuck-file list (same shape as the global read).

SessionEnrichmentSubtaskRead.title: SessionEnrichmentSubtaskRead
SessionEnrichmentSubtaskRead.description:
One per-import sub-task nested under the global enrichment task (#153): a
COMMITTED session whose enrichment is not yet complete. `label` is the
session's root paths joined (or `Import #<id>`), so the Tasks view can render
the global enrichment task with each import's progress underneath it.

SetupRequest.title: SetupRequest
SetupRequest.description: `POST /api/v1/setup` -- create the first admin (setup mode only).

SetupStatusRead.title: SetupStatusRead
SetupStatusRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/setup-status` -- drives the first-run wizard AND, unauthenticated,
the login screen (so it can show an "Explore the demo" entry before any auth).

SimilarCard.title: SimilarCard
SimilarCard.description:
DETAILDATA-BE: one lightweight "more like this" card (TMDB `/similar`).

The unified detail view (preview + library) renders a poster rail of these;
each carries just enough to draw a poster and deep-link to that title's own
detail (preview if not yet in the library). `in_library` is kind-scoped, the
same (kind, tmdb_id) identity dedup uses everywhere else.

SystemStatusRead.title: SystemStatusRead
SystemStatusRead.description:
`GET /api/v1/system/status` (LF-V1) -- arr-parity-ish, read-only.

Minimal today (app name + version); a natural place to grow additional
read-only runtime facts later without touching `/health`'s shape.

SystemTaskRead.title: SystemTaskRead
SystemTaskRead.description:
ST-B1: one scheduled background task (``GET /api/v1/system/tasks``).

Surfaces the scheduler's live per-task metadata at arr ``/system/task``
parity: the registered ``name``, its (live-resolved) ``interval_seconds``,
whether a run is in flight (``running``), the ``last_run`` timestamp +
``last_duration`` (seconds) + ``last_result`` outcome, and the ``next_run``
the UI counts down to.

TmdbTestResult.title: TmdbTestResult
TmdbTestResult.description:
LF-B4: result of `POST /api/v1/settings/test-tmdb`. Never echoes the
key -- only a boolean and a human-readable message.

TokenCreate.title: TokenCreate
TokenCreate.description:
`POST /api/v1/tokens` -- mint a personal API token.

`expires_at` is optional (a null/absent value never expires). `user_id`
lets a `users.manage` holder mint a token ON BEHALF OF another user; a
self-service caller omits it (or passes their own id). See the route's
`_authz_target` for the admin-any authorization.

TokenMintRead.title: TokenMintRead
TokenMintRead.description:
The one-time mint response: `TokenRead` metadata PLUS the raw `token`.

`token` is `"<prefix>_<secret>"` -- the ONLY time the secret is ever
returned. It is not persisted (only a SHA-256 of the secret is), so it
cannot be recovered later; the caller must store it now.

TokenRead.title: TokenRead
TokenRead.description:
A personal API token's non-secret metadata.

Carries NO `token_hash` and NO secret -- the raw token is never present in
this DTO, only ever in `TokenMintRead.token` at mint time. `token_prefix`
is the non-secret lookup half of the raw token, safe to display so a user
can recognise which token a row is.

TrashAnimePreferences.title: TrashAnimePreferences
TrashAnimePreferences.description:
TRASH-F: anime preference toggles. Each maps to a score nudge on the
imported anime CFs it matches — dual-audio / uncensored / English-dub
releases scored up, raw/low-quality groups scored down — applied
override-safe (a hand-retuned score is left alone).

TrashAnimePreferencesResult.title: TrashAnimePreferencesResult
TrashAnimePreferencesResult.description:
`PUT /trash/anime-preferences` echo: the persisted toggles plus how many
anime CF scores the change nudged.

TrashCatalogEntry.title: TrashCatalogEntry
TrashCatalogEntry.description: #37: one custom format in the searchable catalog (`GET /trash/catalog`).

TrashCatalogRead.title: TrashCatalogRead
TrashCatalogRead.description: #37: `GET /trash/catalog` payload -- the category's CFs + group sidebar.

TrashConflict.title: TrashConflict
TrashConflict.description:
One local override that diverges from the latest guide (#11).

Auto-sync PRESERVES this override (never clobbers it); this record makes the
preserved-vs-guide delta visible so the user can consciously **Accept guide**
(`POST /customformats/{cf_id}/reset`) or **Keep mine** (no-op).

TrashConflictSpec.title: TrashConflictSpec
TrashConflictSpec.description: One normalised custom-format specification (#11 conflict view).

TrashConflictsRead.title: TrashConflictsRead
TrashConflictsRead.description:
`POST /trash/conflicts`: every local override that now diverges from the
guide. Empty when nothing diverges.

TrashGroupCount.title: TrashGroupCount
TrashGroupCount.description: #37: one cf-group entry in the catalog sidebar (name + CF count).

TvdbSearchResult.title: TvdbSearchResult
TvdbSearchResult.description:
#180 Phase 3: a TVDB series search candidate for the Add/Discover flow's
"not on TMDB?" path. `tvdb_id` is the identity; `tmdb_id` is populated only
when the candidate ALSO carries a TMDB remote id (so the UI can prefer the
normal TMDB add for it). `image_url` is an ABSOLUTE TVDB URL (rendered
directly, unlike the TMDB-relative poster paths). A separate DTO from
`MediaSearchResult` because that one requires a non-null `tmdb_id`, which a
genuinely tmdb-less candidate cannot supply.

TvdbTestResult.title: TvdbTestResult
TvdbTestResult.description:
#180: result of `POST /api/v1/settings/test-tvdb`. Never echoes the key
or PIN -- only a boolean and a human-readable message.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description:
`POST /api/v1/users` -- admin-created account (CA-1).

`password` is write-only: it is hashed on the way in and never echoed
back (`UserRead` carries no password field), so there is no read-side
secret to redact here. `role_id` optionally assigns an RBAC role at
creation (validated to exist; `is_admin` is then synced from the role).

UserRead.title: UserRead
UserRead.description:
A user account, sans password hash (never exposed).

``role_id``/``role_name`` name the user's assigned RBAC role (both ``None``
when unassigned); ``permissions`` is the resolved Axis-A permission set the
role confers (empty for the Viewer/no-role case). All three are additive and
backward-compatible -- an older client reading only ``id``/``username``/
``is_admin`` is unaffected.

UserRequestPolicyRead.title: UserRequestPolicyRead
UserRequestPolicyRead.description:
A user's request policy. Tier lists carry `QualityTier` values; an EMPTY
`allowed_tiers` means no restriction (all tiers). `quota_per_week` null =
unlimited. `request_quality_mode` is the P2a admin quality mode: `choose`
(the user picks access-scoped editions) or `auto` (an admin-fixed set).

UserRequestPolicyUpdate.title: UserRequestPolicyUpdate
UserRequestPolicyUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/v1/users/{user_id}/request-policy` — upsert the policy. Absent
fields keep their stored value; tier names are validated against
`QualityTier`.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}` -- rename / (de)promote / (re)assign role (CA-1).

Password is deliberately NOT settable here -- it changes only through the
dedicated `change-password` action (current-password verified). `role_id`
(re)assigns an RBAC role; setting it re-syncs the `is_admin` column from the
target role's permissions.

VapidPublicKeyRead.title: VapidPublicKeyRead
VapidPublicKeyRead.description: The non-secret VAPID application-server public key (base64url).

VapidRotateResult.title: VapidRotateResult
VapidRotateResult.description: The outcome of a VAPID keypair rotation.

WantedEdition.title: WantedEdition
WantedEdition.description:
The Wanted state of ONE monitored edition of a title.

``state`` is the per-edition verdict:

* ``missing``      -- grabbable now but no file (a released movie edition, or
  a series edition with >=1 aired monitored fileless episode);
* ``cutoff_unmet`` -- a file exists but below the profile's cutoff quality;
* ``upcoming``     -- monitored + fileless but NOT yet grabbable (an
  unreleased movie stage for the allowed qualities, or a series edition
  whose only outstanding episodes have not aired) -- it lives on the
  Calendar, not the actionable backlog;
* ``have``         -- fully satisfied (file at/above cutoff).

Only ``missing`` / ``cutoff_unmet`` editions make a title appear on the
Wanted list; ``upcoming`` / ``have`` editions ride along for context.

WantedItem.title: WantedItem
WantedItem.description:
One title on the Wanted list (grouped -- a single entry even when several
of its editions are wanted). ``kind`` + ``is_anime`` + ``series_type``
classify it into the movies / series / anime buckets; ``editions`` carries
the per-edition state.

WantedMissingEpisode.title: WantedMissingEpisode
WantedMissingEpisode.description:
One specific aired-but-missing monitored episode of a series edition, so
the Wanted screen can nest the exact episodes under the series edition
(rather than only a count). ``air_datetime`` is the precise broadcast instant
(aware UTC) when TVmaze has enriched it; ``air_date`` is the TMDB date
fallback for display.

WantedMissingMoviePagedResource.title: WantedMissingMoviePagedResource
WantedMissingMoviePagedResource.description:
Radarr v3 `GET /wanted/missing` envelope (#58): the standard arr paged
shape carrying MovieResource records.

WantedPage.title: WantedPage
WantedPage.description:
Paged Wanted feed. ``total`` is the number of TITLE entries (paging is
per-title now that editions are grouped). ``missing_count`` /
``cutoff_unmet_count`` / ``upcoming_count`` are the library-wide edition
tallies (they count editions across every wanted title, not just this page).
``missing_titles`` / ``cutoff_unmet_titles`` / ``upcoming_titles`` are the same
counts at TITLE granularity (a title counted once per state) — these drive the
tab badges so they match each tab's per-title paged feed + footer, which never
disagree on a multi-edition title.

WebPushKeys.title: WebPushKeys
WebPushKeys.description: The device's push encryption keys (base64url) the browser hands us.

WebPushSettingsRead.title: WebPushSettingsRead
WebPushSettingsRead.description: The global Web Push channel policy (admin).

WebPushSettingsUpdate.title: WebPushSettingsUpdate
WebPushSettingsUpdate.description: Edit the global Web Push channel policy (admin). All fields optional.

WildcardGrantCreate.title: WildcardGrantCreate
WildcardGrantCreate.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/grants`` -- a WILDCARD grant (capabilities on ALL
instances). No ``instance_id``; the per-instance grant keeps its own route.

_QueueBulkIds.title: _QueueBulkIds
_QueueBulkIds.description:
Body of ``DELETE /queue/bulk`` -- the queue-record (``Download`` PK) ints
decypharr's Path 1 mutation targets. Module-level (not nested in the router
factory) so FastAPI resolves it as a request body, not a query param.
